items.body:
# Windows command-safety treats a PowerShell parameter value as a URL launcher

This report contains no session transcripts, runtime logs, screenshots, attachments, business URLs, account identifiers, credentials or local user paths.

## Runtime and observed failure

Installed runtime: Codex CLI `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`, Windows, approval policy `never`, approvals reviewer `user`, sandbox `danger-full-access`.

A metadata-only PowerShell helper was rejected before process creation with `blocked by policy`. Its `-Stage` parameter had the literal value `Start`, and a separate `-TargetUrl` parameter held an HTTPS URL. Browser navigation would have been a separate native tool operation after admission; the helper itself does not launch the URL.

The following is descriptive token data, not an instruction to execute a command:

```json
["pwsh", "-File", "<metadata-only-helper.ps1>", "-Stage", "Start", "-TargetUrl", "https://example.invalid/catalog"]
```

## Matching-version static finding

Static inspection of published tag `rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2` shows that the Windows URL-launch predicate combines any HTTP(S) word with any launch-marker word. The argument value `Start` therefore matches this predicate.

- Classifier: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/shell-command/src/command_safety/windows_dangerous_commands.rs#L34
- Policy decision: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/core/src/exec_policy.rs#L759

This matches the observed refusal, but is not an internal trace of the running binary's matched rule. The exact compilation commit of the installed binary has not been separately established.

## Requested supported resolution

Please review this suspected false positive and distinguish a PowerShell command invocation from an argument value without weakening detection of actual URL-launch commands. Keep real `Start-Process`, `start`, `saps`, `Invoke-Item` and `ii` URL launches under the intended policy. Paired regression cases should cover metadata-only argument values and actual URL-launch commands, including the `never` decision path.

Please provide a supported product fix or a documented review path for this specific built-in refusal. This is not a request to change the account's policy, add an allow rule, bypass safeguards or approve an unrelated action.

An exact-version experimental schema contains `thread/approveGuardianDeniedAction`, requiring a serialized `GuardianAssessmentEvent`. No genuine such event was provided for this `never`/`user` pre-exec refusal; that method was not invoked and no event was fabricated.

No rejected command or equivalent was retried. No rules, runtime policy, Desktop lifecycle, browser sessions or credentials were changed. No logs or sessions are attached to this report.

items.title: [Dots][MCP Events] Event-triggered task receives payload but does not send a visible reply

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: dots
labels.description: Issues involving setting up ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work.

items.body:
### App version

Exact desktop About-dialog version was not collected. Task configuration and missing visible replies were also inspected in ChatGPT web in Chrome. This report concerns a cloud-hosted Dot event-monitoring task, not a local Codex CLI task.

### Subscription

Not included in this public report; available privately if needed.

### Platform

macOS, Darwin 25.6.0, arm64. ChatGPT web in Chrome was used for the read-only investigation.

### Summary

A custom MCP Events subscription successfully delivers `alert.created` events to a Dot. Across three distinct test events, the server records first-attempt HTTP 200 responses. The Dot's subsequent read-only diagnostics report updated task last-run times and receipt of the original event payloads, but no visible automatic alert reply appears in the Dot's ChatGPT conversation before the user asks about it.

The third test reduced the action to sending only the title and event ID, with no detail query or dependency on other data. It still produced no automatic reply.

### Steps for the observed occurrences

1. Connect an OAuth-authenticated custom MCP server exposing tools and `alert.created`, using MCP protocol version `2026-07-28`.
2. Ask the Dot to subscribe to that event and post a visible reply in the current ChatGPT conversation. Use the authorized route scope without additional event filters. Subscription/callback verification succeeds.
3. Send a new, uniquely identified signed event with route `base`, severity `info`, and status `test`.
4. Verify that the event callback returns HTTP 200. Do not manually run the task or prompt the Dot while observing whether it replies.
5. When no reply appears, ask the Dot for read-only diagnostics: task enabled state, last-run time, and evidence of the original event payload. Do not replay events, rebuild subscriptions, or manually run the task.
6. Repeat with two new event IDs. Before the third occurrence, simplify the saved task to: immediately post "Received production alert: <title>; eventId: <eventId>", use `data.title` and the top-level `eventId`, report missing fields, do not query details or wait for other data, and include `test`/`info` events.

This is an observed three-occurrence reproduction, not proof of a universally deterministic failure. The original prompts and notifications were in Chinese; the wording above is an English paraphrase.

### Timeline

All dates below are **2026-10-18 UTC** (2026-10-19 in Asia/Shanghai).

| Test | Event occurrence | Callback evidence | Task last-run time reported by Dot diagnostics |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 17:46:30 | First attempt, HTTP 200; application success log at 17:46:33.839 | 17:46:51 |
| B | 17:53:04 | First attempt, HTTP 200; application success log at 17:53:07.558 | 17:53:24.147 |
| C | 18:05:02 | First attempt, HTTP 200 | 18:05:23.078471 |

Each test had a different event ID. They used the same existing subscription and task. Full task/subscription/event IDs, the production hostname, account details and private chat history are omitted from this public report. They can be supplied through a private support channel for correlation.

### Additional clue from test C: waiting before payload arrival

**Evidence limitation:** The following sequence is the Dot's own read-only account of its visible context. We do not have a raw platform execution trace, independent tool timestamps, or a run ID linking each operation. Please treat it as a diagnostic lead, not a proven internal failure mechanism.

The Dot reported this order:

1. An automation request near **18:05:11 UTC** explicitly requested an immediate visible message.
2. A `functions.exec` call waited 1,000 ms using `setTimeout`, then returned completed with no output.
3. A `clock.wait` call with `seconds=1` returned `status=scheduled`. The Dot reported no visible completion callback for that wait.
4. An `automations.mcp_event` payload then appeared containing test C's original event ID, title, internal record ID, route, severity, status and timestamp. The Dot explicitly distinguished this original payload from the ID later included in the user's diagnostic question.
5. Before the user's diagnostic request at **18:07:19 UTC**, the Dot reported no visible subsequent message-send call, send receipt, or final alert output.

The payload timestamp is the event occurrence time, **not** a measurement of when the model received it. A task last-run timestamp is also not proof of execution completion.

### Confirmed observations versus unknowns

**Directly checked outside the Dot's self-report:**
- All three callback deliveries are `sent`, HTTP 200, one attempt each in the server's delivery records.
- The existing ordinary notification channel also delivered each test successfully.
- The saved task remains enabled and its latest simplified instructions are present in the web UI.
- The simplified instructions still explicitly name `user_message.send_message`; the Dot included that name when saving the task.
- The visible Dot conversation contains no automatic alert report for these three tests before the respective diagnostic questions.
- The read-only diagnosis did not manually run the task or resend events.

**Reported by the Dot, not independently verified against platform logs:**
- The task's last-run time advanced for each event.
- The original event payloads reached its context.
- The waiting sequence above and lack of subsequent send evidence for test C.

**Unknown:**
- Per-run completion/failure state, full tool trace and backend errors.
- Whether the automatic run had `user_message.send_message` available, attempted it, or was blocked. Current interactive tool availability does not establish background-run availability.
- Whether event arrival resumed execution after waiting, whether an output was suppressed/routed elsewhere, or whether batching/deduplication played a role.

HTTP 200 is reported only as webhook receipt, not as proof of task completion or user-message delivery. No specific cause is asserted.

### Expected behavior

A matching accepted event should be processed and the configured visible reply delivered without another human message. If the run cannot proceed or send a message, expose an actionable failure state rather than leaving only an advanced last-run timestamp.

### Questions for maintainers

- Can the task/event identifiers supplied privately be correlated with run IDs, tool calls, errors and final outputs?
- If the automation request and `automations.mcp_event` arrive separately, is execution reliably resumed after the payload arrives, including after a scheduled wait?
- What is the supported way for a Dot event task to publish into its main ChatGPT conversation? Should saved task instructions avoid naming internal tools?
- What supported diagnostics can expose the failure boundary without publishing private chat history or credentials?

### Related report

#50714 describes MCP webhook runs lacking the `automations.mcp_event` payload. In this case, the Dot later reports the original payload is present, but no automatic visible response follows. The symptoms may be related; a common cause has not been established.

Submitted with the user's explicit authorization. No credentials, callback secrets, production domain or full private identifiers are included.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

0.163.0.

### What subscription do you have?

Pro 100

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 PRo

### What issue are you seeing?

Part 1 of 6 — Reasoning/Debugging Regression After Usage Reset
I am reporting a significant change in the reasoning and debugging performance of ChatGPT Work/Codex that appeared immediately after a usage reset.
I use ChatGPT Work extensively for a large, long-running software development project. My current configuration is GPT-6.1 Sol Medium on a Pro subscription.
I maintain detailed handoff information in Open Brain (OB), and the full results of debugging and development sessions are also retained on my local system. This gives each new session substantial context and makes it possible to distinguish a context-loss problem from a more general reasoning-performance problem.
Before the recent usage reset, Work/Codex was generally able to maintain the debugging objective, follow evidence through complex problems, and make steady progress.
After the usage reset, its behavior changed noticeably.
________________________________________
Part 2 of 6 — What Changed
During debugging, Work will sometimes appear to become “lost.” It stops efficiently pursuing the original problem, repeats or revisits work unnecessarily, follows less productive branches, and can take substantially longer to reach conclusions that previously would have been handled efficiently.
Importantly, this is not limited to starting a new session.
I have observed the degradation within an active session, even after the model has already loaded the relevant context and has been working correctly on the problem.
This distinction is important because the problem cannot simply be attributed to a fresh session not having enough context.
The model can begin a debugging session correctly, understand the objective and evidence, and then later lose the thread of the investigation or begin pursuing unnecessary paths.
________________________________________
Part 3 of 6 — Usage Behavior and Model Comparison
After only about two days following the reset, my usage allowance had already fallen to approximately 23% remaining. That level of consumption is unusually fast compared with my prior experience.
The increased usage appears consistent with the debugging inefficiency I am seeing: the model performs considerably more reasoning/work to accomplish tasks that previously required much less.
I upgraded to Pro and have been using GPT-6.1 Sol Medium.
Last week, because of usage limits, Work switched me back to GPT-5.6 High. I did not observe the same degree of debugging/reasoning difficulty during that period.
The severe degradation became particularly noticeable after the subsequent usage reset.
This makes me concerned that something other than the model name displayed in the interface may be changing with usage state.
________________________________________
Part 4 of 6 — Why This Does Not Appear to Be Missing Context
For my development workflow:
• Handoff notes are stored in Open Brain.
• Detailed debugging results and evidence are preserved.
• Full results are also retained on my local machine.
• I routinely start new sessions from explicit handoff records.
• The problem can occur after a session is already underway, not just during initial context loading.
Because of this, the behavior does not appear to be explained solely by a new session lacking context.
Observed symptoms include losing track of the primary debugging objective, re-examining already-established facts, pursuing unnecessary branches, and requiring substantially more reasoning and usage for comparable work.
The degradation can occur during an established Work/Codex session after the system has already demonstrated that it understands the problem.
________________________________________
Part 5 of 6 — Why I Believe This Is a Regression
This appears to be a reasoning-performance regression or a change in runtime/model behavior associated with the usage reset, rather than ordinary variation in response quality.
Because Work is being used for a substantial software-development project, the difference is very noticeable.
I have historical development runs, handoff records, test results, and local artifacts that make it possible to compare behavior before and after the reset.
I have also seen reports from other developers describing a similar pattern: following resets or changes in usage state, coding/debugging agents appear less efficient, lose the objective more easily, and consume considerably more time or reasoning to complete the same kind of work.
I recognize those reports are anecdotal, but the similarity to what I am directly observing is concerning.
________________________________________
Part 6 of 6 — Requested Engineering Investigation
Could the OpenAI engineering team please investigate whether any of the following change when a Pro user's usage allocation resets or crosses usage thresholds:
1.	Model routing or model variant.
2.	Reasoning budget or reasoning policy.
3.	Context handling or context compression.
4.	Tool-use planning behavior.
5.	Work/Codex agent configuration.
6.	Runtime resource allocation.
7.	Adaptive throttling or other usage-related quality controls.
8.	Differences between GPT-6.1 Sol Medium and GPT-5.6 High in Work/Codex after a reset.
I would particularly appreciate confirmation of whether a usage reset can cause any change in effective model configuration or reasoning behavior, even when the model shown in the interface remains the same.
I can provide specific session examples, Open Brain handoff records, debugging timelines, usage information, test results, and other evidence if engineering would find them useful.



### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Feedback ID: 01a14c6a-f765-74d1-86f4-2a3b6036c221

### What is the expected behavior?

Thinking logic and less round trips for the same debugging session. All coding specifications and review is taking substantially longer than expected and going through tokens much quicker. Before the reset, I would be able to use work most of the week at 6.1 Sol and Codex at 6.1 Sol. I went through 73% of usage after the reset. 

### Additional information

_No response_

## Environment
- ChatGPT desktop app on Windows, using Work with the bundled Computer Use plugin.
- Bundled Computer Use skill/plugin path version: `26.1013.40934`. This is the plugin version, not a verified desktop app version.
- Codex CLI: 0.163.0. Exact desktop app build and Windows version were not independently established during this diagnosis.
- Target: an existing MediaPortal 1.39 x64 installation (`MediaPortal.exe`).
- Observed October 18, 2026, approximately 19:39–20:01 Europe/Berlin.

## Problem
The owner repeatedly selects **Always allow this app**, and also tried approval for the conversation. Computer Use still prompts repeatedly to allow ChatGPT to use `mediaportal`. Individual activation/keyboard actions sometimes succeed, then later actions fail with:

`Computer Use was not approved to use mediaportal`

The owner checked **Settings > Computer use > Always-allowed apps**: MediaPortal is absent despite repeatedly selecting Always allow. The owner sees no option to add it manually.

## Observed sequence
1. The owner starts the installed MediaPortal manually; Titan Home renders normally.
2. Computer Use enumerates and captures the returned MediaPortal window successfully.
3. Activation/input requests show the per-app approval dialog.
4. The owner selects Always allow, repeatedly.
5. Some activation and keyboard navigation succeeds, but later actions request approval again or return the error above.
6. MediaPortal remains absent from Always-allowed apps.

The returned app identifier remained the same installed MediaPortal executable path during the successful and denied interactions; the report omits the full path. Automation was paused to stop generating more prompts. No permission store, security setting, or app data was modified or reset.

## Read-only diagnostic evidence
In the inspected desktop logs for 17:38–17:59 UTC, there are **19 `Responding to ChatGPT Computer Use app approval` events**:
- 5 with `action=allow persist=always`
- 14 with `action=allow persist=session`

These contain 18 distinct request identifiers; one identifier received two replies. Identifiers are omitted. This confirms the frontend recorded approval selections; it does **not** prove backend persistence or that every log event has been independently correlated to this target.

No matching `Unrecognized MCP message` or explicit approval-persistence failure was found in that inspected interval. Nearby `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` messages were present, but no causal relationship is established.

## Expected
Always allow should persist the target app approval and avoid asking again for routine authorized navigation. If the approval cannot be saved/applied, the UI should explain why and settle the request rather than repeatedly presenting a nonfunctional choice.

## Related report
Possibly related symptom: #51838 (macOS/connected-runtime approval loop). This Windows case has not reproduced the protocol errors in that report, so a shared root cause is unconfirmed.

Please investigate the Windows ChatGPT Computer Use approval persistence/application path and advise on a supported recovery that preserves existing chats and settings.

Prepared with AI assistance at the owner's explicit request. No raw logs, screenshots, private project contents, account details, conversation IDs, request IDs, credentials, or private repository links are attached.

items.title: Windows: Git marketplace clone triggers git.exe / git-remote-https.exe 0xC0000142 dialogs

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Verified installed Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64` (the running executable is named `ChatGPT.exe`).
Bundled CLI/app-server executable reports: `codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2`.

These versions were recorded on 2026-10-18. The intermittent failures have been observed across several days and earlier app versions.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected. The verified evidence below concerns local Windows subprocess initialization and marketplace synchronization.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64. Latest verified OS version string: `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0`.
Earlier checks on the same machine returned build 26200.
Git for Windows: `git version 2.56.0.windows.2`.

### What issue are you seeing?

Recurring Windows application-error dialogs for `git.exe` and `git-remote-https.exe`, with status `0xc0000142` (DLL initialization failure), during use of the Codex desktop app.

At least one occurrence was correlated with a Git-backed plugin marketplace clone using Microsoft Sysinternals Process Monitor. The repository being cloned was `https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-mcp.git`.

Observed on 2026-10-18, Europe/Paris (UTC+02:00):
- 17:14:25: Process Monitor showed `git.exe` PID 30212 executing a command beginning:
  `git.exe -c safe.bareRepository=explicit clone https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-mcp.git <Codex-managed target>`
- 17:14:26: a child `git.exe` PID 47592 had command line:
  `git remote-https origin https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-mcp.git`
- The trace showed the system Git implementation under:
  `C:\Program Files\Git\ucrt64\libexec\git-core\git.exe`
- 17:14:26.063464: Windows System log recorded an `Application Popup`, event ID 26, for `git.exe` with `0xc0000142`. The popup was also visible alongside the trace.
- At 19:34:25.726806, the System log recorded another `0xc0000142` popup for `git-remote-https.exe`.

Exact Windows message (French):
> L’application n’a pas réussi à démarrer correctement (0xc0000142). Cliquez sur OK pour fermer l’application.

Updating Git did not stop the recurring dialogs. Standalone read-only tests of `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe --version` succeeded on multiple occasions, including after the failures. That demonstrates intermittency, not a successful reproduction outside Codex.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The failure is intermittent; a deterministic minimal reproduction has not been established.

Observed setup and sequence:
1. Codex desktop on Windows has a configured Git marketplace:
   ```toml
   [marketplaces.drawio]
   source_type = "git"
   source = "https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-mcp.git"
   ```
2. Leave the desktop app running and use it normally.
3. During a marketplace-cloning attempt, Git subprocess startup can fail with a modal Windows `0xc0000142` dialog.
4. The user removed the Draw.io plugin through the app, but a later configuration inspection still found the marketplace source above. No Draw.io plugin entry or Draw.io MCP server entry was found in that user configuration, and no matching Draw.io MCP process was detected in the process check.
5. The remaining marketplace source was subsequently removed using the supported command:
   `codex plugin marketplace remove drawio --json`.
   It returned `marketplaceName: drawio` and a root under `<CODEX_HOME>\.tmp\marketplaces\drawio`. A configuration recheck found no remaining Draw.io references.

The removal was performed on 2026-10-18 after the last listed failure. There is not yet sufficient follow-up to claim that it fixes the Git initialization problem.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Git-backed marketplace synchronization should run reliably on Windows, or report a bounded, actionable failure in the app rather than recurring native application-error dialogs.
- Please clarify the intended lifecycle when the last plugin from a manually configured marketplace is uninstalled. If retaining and refreshing its Git source is intentional, the UI should make that distinction and the way to remove the source clear.
- Please investigate the environment/process-creation context used for marketplace Git children, and whether repeated synchronization after a child-initialization failure is handled appropriately.

### Additional information

Windows System / Application Popup / event ID 26 recorded these additional failures (Europe/Paris):
- 2026-10-12 21:42:40: `git-remote-https.exe`
- 2026-10-12 21:52:40: `git.exe`
- 2026-10-14 22:28:12: `git-remote-https.exe`
- 2026-10-15 13:54:51: `git.exe`
- 2026-10-16 10:35:17: `git-remote-https.exe`
- 2026-10-16 10:45:19: `git.exe`
- 2026-10-17 15:41:44: `git.exe`
- 2026-10-18 12:54:25 and 13:29:25: `git-remote-https.exe`

All listed dialogs carried `0xc0000142`.

Evidence limitations:
- The 17:14 incident was observed in a Process Monitor capture and correlated to the System event, including the clone URL, command lines and executable path. A complete launcher-parent chain was not exported.
- Other occurrences are confirmed by Windows events, but were not individually attributed to the same marketplace.
- No root cause has been established in Codex, Git, a particular DLL, the sandbox, or Windows. No claim is made that the Draw.io MCP implementation itself is faulty.
- Retaining the marketplace after plugin removal is a confirmed configuration observation; whether that behavior is a defect or intended independent marketplace tracking needs maintainer clarification.
- No memory-exhaustion or non-interactive-session mechanism has been demonstrated for this incident.

Potentially related reports, with different observed contexts:

items.body:
## Observed behavior

In a macOS desktop chat using a managed workspace-write runtime with automatic review, an explicitly authorized production configuration action was denied before process creation. Its consent had been transferred from a controller chat to an execution chat, and the denial rationale did not accept the transferred consent as trusted direct user authorization. The reviewer's complete internal inputs are unknown; this report does not establish the cause of that classification.

After reading the current official desktop slash-command documentation, the human user entered `/approve` in the same execution chat. It arrived as an ordinary user message. No native recent-denials picker appeared, as confirmed by the human user, and the agent received no native approval outcome.

No rejected production action was retried after this test. No approval/sandbox policy, credentials or production resources were changed.

## Observed sequence

1. An action in the desktop chat is rejected by automatic review before process creation.
2. The user enters `/approve` in the same chat.
3. The command appears as ordinary conversation text.
4. The user confirms that no native denial picker appeared.

This is a retained observation, not an independently reproduced minimal test. No additional production action was submitted merely to reproduce it.

## Expected behavior / questions

The desktop slash-command reference documents `/approve` as allowing a user to approve one retry of a recent automatic-review denial, subject to environment and access.

- Is this available for managed desktop execution chats?
- If availability depends on app version, workspace policy, rollout or retained denial state, how can a user identify the applicable condition?
- What supported native review route should be used for an eligible previously denied action?
- How should controller-to-execution consent provenance be supplied without disabling review or changing execution context?

Any retry should remain subject to applicable review. We are not requesting an automatic override or broader permissions.

## Environment

- Desktop chat on macOS with local command-execution tools.
- Runtime: workspace-write; approvals reviewer: auto_review.
- Installed desktop app version and exact macOS version: not collected.
- The rejected command never started. This was not an HTTP permission error from the target service.
- The agent cannot inspect the desktop app's own UI through the available computer-use tool; the missing picker is the user's report.

- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/slash-commands
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing/auto-review

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49439

These appear related by symptom; a shared root cause has not been established.

This public report omits email addresses, production hostnames, credentials, local paths, account/session identifiers and raw conversation logs. Private evidence is retained locally and has not been uploaded. Please identify an official private channel if maintainers need additional diagnostics.

items.body:
## Summary
On Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (build 19045), Codex CLI 0.163.0 completes elevated Windows sandbox provisioning, but a minimal sandboxed command fails before execution with `CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 2` (`The system cannot find the file specified`). Reproduces even when the executable is specified by absolute path.

## Environment
- Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045, x86-64
- Codex CLI 0.163.0, official OpenAI-signed standalone binary
- Matching official signed Windows sandbox setup helper and command runner, installed under `C:\Program Files\Codex-Trusted`
- Windows sandbox accounts: `CodexSandboxOffline`, `CodexSandboxOnline` (both enabled and reporting OK)

## Reproduction
1. Install verified official Codex CLI 0.163.0 and matching sandbox helper.
2. Run official elevated sandbox provisioning for the current Windows account; setup reports success.
3. From normal PowerShell, run:

```powershell
& 'C:\Program Files\Codex-Trusted\codex.exe' sandbox windows --full-auto -- 'C:\Windows\System32\whoami.exe'
```

## Actual
```text
windows sandbox failed: runner failed during SpawnChild:
CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 2 (The system cannot find the file specified.)
```
The command never starts. Also reproduced using `cmd /c whoami` and from `C:\Windows\Temp`.

## Expected
The sandbox launches the requested executable and prints the sandbox account identity.

## Diagnostics already performed
- Verified the Codex CLI, setup helper and command runner are official signed binaries; command runner signature valid.
- Confirmed both sandbox local accounts are enabled, status OK.
- Confirmed both sandbox accounts do **not** have registered Windows user profiles (observation; causal link unproven).
- Verified `whoami.exe` exists and current working directory exists.
- Verified the command runner and installation directory grant read/execute access to Users and application package principals.
- Checked Windows User Profile Service and Code Integrity operational logs; no event directly matching the sandbox launch failure identified.
- `SystemRoot`, `WINDIR`, `ComSpec` and `PATH` are populated normally.
- No Windows security protections or ACLs were weakened.

## Request
What path/dependency is missing at `CreateProcessAsUserW`, and is sandbox user profile initialization or Windows 10 compatibility implicated? Is there a supported diagnostic/fix that preserves sandbox security?

## Related reports
- #44783: similar `CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 2` after successful provisioning, but on Windows 11 / CLI 0.154.0
- #43313 and #36386: related process-launch failures

This report adds a Windows 10 build 19045 reproduction on CLI 0.163.0.

## Summary

## Environment and version confidence

## Observed operation sequence

1. A public documentation tab was available at https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/tabGroups .
2. Native Chrome state inspection initially worked during the wider workflow. A normal extension-triggered refresh prompt was observed with its refresh button focused.
3. The subsequent native key/action call timed out. Delivery of that key and completion of the refresh could not be confirmed; no duplicate input was sent.
4. Later native Chrome AX reads, screenshot requests and reconnection after a normal REPL reset also timed out.
5. In a later bounded control, `cua.listApps({emit:false})` succeeded in 352 ms and identified Chrome as running. `cua.getApp("com.google.Chrome")` then returned the timeout in 5.1505 seconds.

```javascript
await cua.getApp("com.google.Chrome");
```

This describes the calls that exposed the boundary. The trigger that turns a working native state read into the failure has not been isolated. Browser DOM success must not be treated as native state-capture success.

## Expected and actual

Expected: native state capture should return the Chrome window state, or an actionable diagnostic identifying the unsupported/failing operation.
Actual: the generic timeout above, while other independent request paths respond.

## Controls and limits

- No claim of a global CUA outage, a confirmed Chrome Accessibility deadlock, or a confirmed permission cause.
- The refresh prompt preceded some failures; causation is unproven.
- Normal REPL reset did not establish recovery. Shared applications were not force-quit and security settings were not changed.

items.title: Hosted Apps connector rejects valid unanchored JSON Schema pattern matches

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

The hosted Apps connector runtime rejects valid string values for an unanchored JSON Schema pattern. This blocks tool calls through Codex before they reach the upstream MCP server.

For a published sender field with `pattern: "\\S"`, the service accepts a single non-whitespace character but rejects longer valid values:

- `"j"`: passes connector validation and reaches the upstream server.
- `"S"`: passes connector validation and reaches the upstream server.
- `"jj"`: rejected with a pattern error.
- `"jellyfish"`: rejected with a pattern error.

Observed error:

```text
Parameters failed connector schema validation: sender.name [pattern]: String does not match pattern '\S'
```

The structured error contains `error_code: "INVALID_ARGUMENT"`, `reason: "INVALID_PARAMETERS"`, a corresponding entry in `clamp_errors`, and an empty `clamp_rewrites` array.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Expose an MCP tool through an Apps connector with this input schema. The sender field below is extracted from the live upstream schema:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "sender": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "name": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1,
          "maxLength": 128,
          "pattern": "\\S",
          "not": { "pattern": "[\\u0000-\\u001f\\u007f]" }
        }
      },
      "required": ["name"],
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  },
  "required": ["sender"]
}
```

2. Call the tool through the hosted connector with `{"sender":{"name":"j"}}`.
3. Repeat with `{"sender":{"name":"jj"}}` and `{"sender":{"name":"jellyfish"}}`.
4. Compare against calls made directly to the upstream MCP server. All three values should pass this field's validation.

The live reproduction used an existing thread-send tool and a target thread confirmed not to exist, so no message was delivered. The original failure affected all three sender fields carrying this pattern: name, project, and source thread ID. It also blocks thread-launch calls.

### What is the expected behavior?

All three values match `\S` under JSON Schema semantics. The pattern requires at least one non-whitespace character somewhere in the value, not exactly one character.

JSON Schema explicitly states that regular expressions are not implicitly anchored:
https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation#section-6.3.3

The nonblank constraint, maximum length, and control-character rejection should remain enforced.

### Additional information

This was isolated to the hosted service, rather than just inferred from a Codex tool error:

- With identical arguments, the direct upstream MCP call accepts the sender fields and returns the expected `thread_not_found` error.
- A separate Python MCP client called `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/ps/mcp` directly using the existing account connection. The server identified itself as `plugin-runtime` version `0.1.0`.
- That direct hosted-service call reproduced the same `clamp_errors` rejection for `"jellyfish"` and `"jj"`, while `"j"` passed validation and reached the upstream server. This bypasses T3 Code, local Codex CLI/app-server, and Codex code mode.
- Codex CLI version at discovery: `0.163.0`, Linux x86_64. The hosted-service reproduction does not depend on model inference.

Codex's matching source identifies this endpoint as the ChatGPT-hosted runtime served by `plugin-service`:
https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/mcp/mod.rs#L620-L649

The observed behavior is consistent with implicit whole-string matching of the JSON Schema pattern. The private backend implementation has not been inspected, so this report does not claim a particular regex function or source location.

Please route this to the hosted Apps/plugin-service connector parameter-validation owner. No gateway schema or production configuration was changed to obtain these results.

MacOS

### What issue are you seeing?

[browser-log-excerpts.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33633231/browser-log-excerpts.txt)

## What happened

The built-in browser could not be opened or controlled by the assistant. The user later manually opened the OpenAI Help Center in a browser tab in the app's right panel, but the tool still returned an empty browser inventory.

Repeated tool results:

```text
cua.listBrowsers() => []

```

This prevented the assistant from completing the authorized support-report submission.

## Steps observed

1. Ask the assistant to open the OpenAI Help Center in the built-in browser.
2. The browser creation call returns the error above and browser discovery returns an empty list.
3. Repeated checks after the user checked permissions, cleared browser history, and closed/reopened the app return the same result.
4. Manually open the Help Center in the app's right-side browser panel; the assistant still discovers no browser.

These are observed troubleshooting steps, not a guaranteed minimal reproduction on another machine.

## Expected behavior

An available in-app browser should be discoverable and controllable by the supported browser tools. If tool access is unavailable, provide a specific reason and recovery path.

## Supporting evidence

Read-only inspection found the browser and unified computer-use plugins enabled, the built-in browser listed among available backends, and Help Center access explicitly allowed. The configured runtime and browser-service files existed when checked.

Desktop logs show browser availability and backend startup success:

```text
2026-10-18T13:44:21.986Z browser_use_availability_resolved available=true browserPane=true platform=macOS reason=available release=26.1013.40934
2026-10-18T13:44:22.117Z browser_use_iab_backend_startup_ready backend=iab platform=darwin release=26.1013.40934
2026-10-18T13:44:30.880Z browser_use_iab_backend_startup_ready backend=iab platform=darwin release=26.1013.40934
```

The same desktop log also records computer-use server startup failures in other chat sessions, including:

```text
MCP client for `cua_repl` failed to start: MCP startup failed: No such file or directory (os error 2)
2026-10-18T13:44:28.624Z warning [AppServerConnection]
MCP client for `cua_repl` failed to start: MCP startup failed: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

Further startup failures occur later in the log, while the reporting voice chat has ready entries. The missing resource was not identified. These failures are diagnostic leads; their causal relationship to the empty browser inventory is unproven. Tool response payloads did not expose exact timestamps, so no precise correlation with individual retries is claimed.

Sanitized supporting file: `browser-log-excerpts.txt`.
Source directory: `~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/2026/10/18/`.

## Assessment and scope

The established problem is a mismatch between desktop/UI browser availability and browser discovery exposed to the assistant. A discovery or session-connection problem is suspected; the root cause is not confirmed.

An earlier attempt to use Safari was separately stopped by a URL policy restriction that did not identify the URL. That restriction is not established to share a cause with this in-app browser issue.

Related voice issue: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/55067. This report is specifically about browser access; a shared cause with the voice problem is not established.

Full conversation transcripts, raw configuration, private URLs, socket paths, and unrelated identifiers are omitted.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Steps to reproduce”:
1. In Codex for macOS, ask the assistant to open the OpenAI Help Center using the built-in browser.
2. The assistant reports an empty browser inventory and the error Browser is not available: iab.
3. Manually open the Help Center in Codex’s browser panel.
4. Ask the assistant to inspect or take a screenshot of that tab. It still reports no browser connection.
5. Allow website access and restart Codex, then retry. In this session, the problem persisted.
6. These describe what happened on my machine; reproducibility on another machine hasn’t been confirmed.

### What is the expected behavior?

The assistant should be able to discover and use the built-in browser when it is available and website access is allowed, including reading the open page and taking screenshots. If browser access is unavailable, the app should explain the specific reason and how to restore it.

### Additional information

I explicitly allowed GitHub and the OpenAI Help Center in the app’s browser settings. Despite those permissions, the assistant’s subsequent checks still returned an empty browser list. I could see and use the browser tab, but the assistant could not read it or take a screenshot.

The visible-browser/empty-discovery symptoms overlap. This report adds startup and availability logs, permission checks for GitHub and the OpenAI Help Center, and observed results after restarting the app and manually opening the browser. A shared underlying cause has not been confirmed, so I’m leaving this issue open for maintainers to compare.

items.title: Let `codex exec` start a detached turn on the shared app-server daemon

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: exec
labels.description: Issues related to the `codex exec` subcommand

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI (version 0.163.0 on macOS)

### What feature would you like to see?

A non-interactive way to start a Codex turn that keeps running after the command returns. For example:

- `codex exec --detach` could start the session and its turn on the shared app-server daemon, print the thread ID, and exit.
- `codex exec resume --detach <thread-id>` would do the same for a follow-up turn.

Per-run options such as `-m`, `-c`, and `--approve-for-me` would apply to that turn as they do today. A matching CLI command to interrupt a running turn on the daemon would complete the lifecycle.

This is related to #23132, which asks for `/detach` in an interactive session. This request covers starting a turn detached, without any TUI.

### Additional information

I run Codex non-interactively from other tools that need to start a turn, keep working, and check on or stop it later. With `codex exec`, that works only if the tool can keep the process alive in the background for the whole turn. Claude Code covers this case with `claude --bg` and `claude stop`.

The shared daemon already keeps a turn running after its client unsubscribes, but nothing non-interactive can start a turn there. `codex exec` runs its own in-process app server and rejects `--remote`. `codex queue` only stores a message for an existing session and can’t set per-turn options.

A custom client for the experimental app-server protocol is an overkill for this use case.

items.body:
### Environment

Observed on 2026-10-19 (JST) in the Windows Codex desktop app.
- Installed MSIX package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.9446.0 (queried read-only with Get-AppxPackage; not asserted to be the About-dialog version).
- Desktop-managed codex.exe: codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 (queried from the actual CODEX_CLI_PATH).
- Windows NT 10.0.26200.0, x64.
- workspace-write sandbox; approvals_reviewer=auto_review.
- Subscription and separate About-dialog version were not collected.

### Problem

An authorized local collaboration workflow is blocked at send_message_to_thread. The owner explicitly allowed the affected executor chat to share nonsecret operational records with two designated existing local chats (the application owner and independent verifier), excluding password/key values and external publication.

Initial forwarded consent was rejected as untrusted. The human then typed the approval directly in the affected, writable executor chat. The native thread reader confirmed a userMessage in that same chat before the next send. Both designated sends were still rejected. The latest rationale said:

> the quoted approval appears only in untrusted retained transcript context and cannot authorize this exact cross-thread disclosure

The other destination was denied with the equivalent reason that the claimed approval existed only in untrusted transcript context. This report preserves that rationale; we cannot determine what context the separate reviewer actually received.

The proposed messages contained local artifact references/checksums, startup/stop-control conditions and mocked test results. They contained no password/key/token values or business-data payload. The destination was another existing local Codex chat; no outside service was the intended destination of the refused messages.

### Observed sequence in the affected session

1. A coordinating chat obtained explicit owner permission for an isolated trial and successor execution, including coordination with existing owners.
2. Nonsecret receipt/control/validation handoffs were refused as insufficiently authorized cross-thread disclosure.
3. A more specific owner approval in the coordinating chat was verified through the native thread reader, but the resulting sends were also refused.
4. The human opened the affected executor chat and directly authorized sharing the nonsecret records with the two designated owners, explicitly excluding password/key values and external transmission.
5. The executor recorded that direct approval and sent the corresponding bounded handoffs through the normal send_message_to_thread tool.
6. Both sends were denied again, treating the authorization as untrusted retained transcript context.
7. Execution remained stopped. No alternate sending channel, fabricated approval marker, permission weakening, source-data changes or denial bypass was used.

This is a retained session-specific observation, not a minimal standalone reproducer. At the time this report was prepared, action-specific native approval through /approve had not yet been completed. See the recovery update below; we do not claim that a native override was ignored.

### Expected behavior / requested investigation

Please investigate why direct user input in the affected chat is not recognized as authorization evidence for these exact designated nonsecret sends. If a separate action-specific approval is mandatory, the denial should clearly identify that requirement and provide a reachable supported approval action. Plain-language confirmation loops should not be presented as a reliable recovery mechanism when they cannot resolve the boundary.

The current desktop slash-command documentation lists /approve. Please clarify how that command applies to denied MCP/app-tool calls in an existing local chat, and what supported recovery is available if the matching action is absent or still denied after native approval.

### Impact

A user-approved engineering trial cannot progress to independent validation or launch. The user has had to repeat approvals across multiple chats and directly asked for this report because the disruption is substantial.

### Related reports / limits

- #50119 concerns forwarded main-chat authorization being treated as untrusted; this observation additionally includes successful direct user input in the affected executor chat.
- #45055 concerns a completed native Guardian override followed by denial; that native override sequence has not been tested here.
- #45115 concerns an inaccessible read-only child approval surface; this affected executor is a separately writable local chat.

Please consolidate if these share a tracked cause. No private project names, usernames, filesystem paths, artifact hashes, chat/session identifiers, screenshots, raw logs, credentials or business content are included. The affected user explicitly requested reporting the problem to OpenAI.

### Recovery update: native approval succeeded

After the report was prepared, the human used the desktop's native exact-action approval flow. Developer-scoped one-retry approval markers were delivered for the denied operations. The executor retried the saved, unchanged argument objects: both designated send_message_to_thread calls succeeded, and this GitHub issue was created successfully. This verifies the native approval/retry path in the affected session. It does not establish why direct plain-text authorization was earlier classified as untrusted, nor guarantee unrelated future sends. No permission weakening or alternate sending route was used.

Please retain the earlier observations as a usability/authorization-provenance report: the repeated plain-text approval requests were ineffective, while the action-specific native approval did resolve the tested block.

## Environment

- macOS `26.6.2`, build `25G83`.

## Observed behavior

When an agent requested a local page in the right-hand browser panel, the user observed an empty **New tab** whose address did not contain the requested URL. Manually entering the same URL, `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`, in that right-hand tab displayed the page successfully.

The native-window behavior above is user-reported. The agent independently verified only the tool requests/responses and that the local page served correctly. The product root cause is not confirmed.

## Workflow and tool evidence

1. Serve a local page at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` on the connected Mac.
2. Request a right-hand browser tab using the supported `open_in_codex` tool:

```json
{
  "placement": "right",
  "target": {
    "type": "browser",
    "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8765/"
  }
}
```

3. The first call used the calling delegated task as its default target. A second call explicitly set `threadId` to the parent/main chat. Both supplied the URL and both returned `status: "queued"` with the respective target thread ID.
4. The user reported the empty New tab and then confirmed that entering the URL manually loaded the page in the right-hand panel.

The first call's default target was different from the desired main chat. The second request corrected that target selection; its queued response still did not confirm completed URL navigation. No actual thread IDs are included here.

## Expected behavior

Open the specified URL in the requested right-hand browser tab. If the target is hidden or navigation cannot yet complete, preserve and apply the requested URL when the queued tab opens, or expose a clear pending/failure state.

## Scope and limits

- Confirmed successful workaround: manual entry of the same localhost URL in the right-hand tab.
- Public HTTPS URLs have not been tested; this report does not claim that all URLs are affected.
- The two queued responses alone do not prove where the URL was lost, whether the queued requests were eventually applied, or whether the cause is task routing, queue processing, or browser-tab navigation.
- No product fix has been verified. No further tab-opening attempts were made after the user had the working page open.
- No task contents, account details, email addresses, local user paths, conversation identifiers, screenshots, or raw logs are attached.

Please investigate the requested-URL handoff through `open_in_codex` and queued right-panel tab creation.

### What variant of Codex are you using?

Personal dot connected to Slack.

### What feature would you like to see?

Please add an opt-in way to continue an engaged Slack thread without mentioning the dot again in every reply.

The current friction is in an ordinary conversation: I mention my dot to start a task, it replies or asks a question, and I have to include another @mention to answer, clarify something, or ask it to continue. That interrupts the natural back-and-forth and makes it easy to leave a reply unnoticed.

Suggested behavior:

2. The owner can opt in to continuing that specific thread without repeated mentions.
3. Further messages from that owner in the same thread reach the dot while this option is active.
4. A visible stop/listening control returns the thread to mention-only mode.
5. Unrelated channel messages, other threads, and other senders remain outside the opt-in scope.

This is a UX feature request, not a claim that current documentation promises automatic replies without mentions. The issue is having to mention the dot on every reply, not a request for periodic polling or reminders.

This would improve conversational continuity without making the dot listen to the entire channel. Existing action permissions and confirmation requirements should remain unchanged.

### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Installed Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0` (read from the running app's package manifest).
Active copied Codex core: `codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2`.
Available bundled Computer Use skill package: `26.1013.40934`; Browser Use: `0.1.0-alpha2`.
The About-dialog version was not separately collected.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 10 Home 22H2, build `19045.7807`, x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

**Computer Use and browser tools repeatedly disconnect or return errors during conversations, preventing agents from finishing UI work.**

The user explicitly reports that **native Computer Use is affected too**: agents invoke Computer Use, then the attempt appears to disconnect immediately or errors out. Similar failures happen with browser tools. Across conversations, agents keep attempting these tools and the workflow repeatedly stalls.

The collected examples below document actual `cua_repl` runtime resets, CDP read timeouts, and Browser Use initialization failures. The broader native Computer Use disconnect symptom is also part of this report, as directly observed by the user; this bounded log sample does not enumerate every native desktop attempt.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence in the affected installation:

1. Ask an agent to perform UI work using Computer Use or browser tools.
2. In one recorded CUA session, Chrome tab access and inspection initially work.
3. Later, reload and inspect that existing tab through `mcp__cua_repl.js`.
4. The call times out and the runtime reports that its kernel was reset.
5. Reacquiring the existing tab through `cua.getTab(existingTabId, { browser: existingBrowserId })` also times out and resets the kernel.
6. Browser Use bootstrap in the same conversation fails separately with the trusted native-pipe error shown below.

These steps describe the captured incident, not a clean-machine or deterministic reproduction. The native Computer Use calls that appear to disconnect immediately are additional user-observed incidents; they should be investigated alongside these recorded runtime failures.

### What is the expected behavior?

Computer Use and browser calls should complete reliably and preserve the session while an agent performs authorized UI work. When a runtime or connection fails, the agent should receive an actionable diagnostic and a supported way to recover, rather than repeatedly invoking tools that disconnect, reset, or error out.

### Additional information

#### Recorded CUA runtime failures

Times below are UTC. The October 18 15:xx entries occurred just after midnight on October 19 in Asia/Seoul (UTC+09:00).

| Tool result time (UTC) | Operation | Actual response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-10-15 23:22:19.437 | CUA download workflow in another conversation | `js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request` (32.4076 s) |
| 2026-10-18 15:46:43.753 | Name an existing browser session, reload its existing tab, then read its AX state | `js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request` (33.0267 s) |
| 2026-10-18 15:47:30.442 | Reacquire the existing tab with `cua.getTab(...)` | `js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request` (34.7531 s) |

Selected read failures from CUA in another conversation on October 16:

```text
2026-10-16T12:10:27.136Z
Timed out after 3000ms waiting for selector internal:role=heading:
Timed out after 3000ms waiting for CDP command Runtime.evaluate.

2026-10-16T12:17:57.177Z
Timed out after 10000ms waiting for CDP command DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot.

2026-10-16T12:21:32.752Z
Timed out after 10000ms waiting for CDP command Page.getFrameTree.
```

#### Separate Browser Use initialization failures

At `2026-10-18T14:33:17.790Z` and `2026-10-18T15:51:35.150Z`, invoking `setupAtlasRuntime({ globals: globalThis })` through Node REPL and the bundled `browser-use/0.1.0-alpha2/scripts/browser-client.mjs` returned:

```text
privileged native pipe bridge is not available; browser-client is not trusted
```

The later tool response explicitly had `isError: true`. These errors occurred while initializing the browser runtime, before it could inspect the intended page.

#### Scope and related reports

- Some CUA calls succeeded between failures. This is intermittent instability, not a claim that every UI call fails.
- The CUA method examples above are browser operations through the Computer Use tool. They support runtime/reset symptoms; they do not independently prove the cause of the user's additional native desktop disconnects.
- Selector misses, an undefined JavaScript variable, and errors in the user's local web app were excluded from the product-failure examples.
- #53456 has similar timeout/reset wording, but its body concerns CLI sandbox provisioning on a different environment. The present report supplies actual CUA timeout/reset responses from the desktop workflow.
- #21781 and #25247 contain the same Browser Use trust error. A shared cause with CUA resets or native Computer Use disconnects is not established.

Please investigate native Computer Use startup/continuation and CUA runtime connection/reset handling as well as Browser Use initialization. The user is experiencing repeated failures across both kinds of UI work.

Only selected error text, operation descriptions, versions, and timestamps are included. Account identifiers, conversation/tab IDs, private URLs, local user paths, project names, credentials, and full transcripts are omitted. ### What version of the Codex App are you using?

ChatGPT/Codex desktop app **26.1013.40934**, build **20770**, read from the installed macOS app metadata. The About dialog was not opened during this investigation.

Affected plugin: **Meetings (Beta), chatgpt-meetings 0.8.92**.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this public report.

### What platform is your computer?

**macOS 27.0.1, arm64**.

Observed on **2026-10-18**. Times below are **UTC+08:00**. MB means 1,000,000 bytes.

### What issue are you seeing?

With Meetings installed, the user reports not using the meeting feature, yet **24–27 concurrent Python MCP workers** were observed and repeated multi-MB downloads occurred in the background. No recording, transcription or meeting-tool action was intentionally started for these measurements.

This report concerns background network usage and worker lifecycle, not a measured high-CPU incident. It does not establish that recording was active or that every byte of the user's overall network usage was caused by Meetings.

#### Process identity

Observed command, with all user-specific paths replaced:

```text
[PYTHON_RUNTIME]/python3.12 -u [PLUGIN_CACHE]/chatgpt-meetings/0.8.92/scripts/meetings_mcp_entrypoint.py --profile production
```

The process chains were:

```text
Meetings Python worker
  <- separate Node Meetings launcher (start_bundled_meetings_mcp.mjs)
  <- the same Codex app-server
  <- ChatGPT desktop host
```

Several snapshots contained 24–26 workers; a later pre-uninstall snapshot contained 27. Some workers were newly created, while others had been running for over a day. The installed-plugin list contained one Meetings installation, not 27 separately installed plugins.

We have not mapped every worker to its owning conversation or established which instances, if any, were orphaned. Multiple instances alone are not being presented as proof of a leak.

#### Four-minute application traffic sample

22:56:05–23:00:09, approximately 240 seconds of polling (243.531 seconds including the final readback):

| Observed category | Download bytes | Upload bytes |
|---|---:|---:|
| Bundled Python runtime, whose contemporaneous same-path processes were Meetings MCP workers | 67,556,204 | 153,071 |
| Codex CLI | 28,312,677 | 4,695,642 |
| Codex Service | 3,297,818 | 2,876,412 |
| Google Drive | 280,635 | 244,252 |
| Whole-machine proxy application counters, including ended connections | 105,898,087 | 9,458,349 |

The Python category had 47 observed connections, predominantly to **chatgpt.com**.

Method: read-only polling of the existing local proxy's connection counters about every 0.2 seconds, subtracting initial counters for already-open connections and retaining each connection's maximum observed increment. Per-application figures are lower bounds because short-lived connections/final increments can be missed. Captured connections represented **96.032%** of the whole-machine transfer counter in this window. These are application-byte observations, not ISP/VPS billing data.

#### Socket-to-PID follow-up: established workers also download again

A separate sample at **23:02:28–23:05:29** mapped local source ports to PIDs and checked the executable/entrypoint. All successfully mapped Python owners were Meetings MCP workers.

Observed download lower bound: **18,447,879 bytes**, upload: **62,373 bytes**.

Examples, with PIDs replaced by neutral worker labels:

- **Worker A:** created at 22:54:34; opened another connection at 23:04:40, approximately **606.6 seconds later**; observed **7,076,512 bytes downloaded** and 3,839 bytes uploaded.
- **Worker B:** an already-running worker opened a new connection approximately **1,817.8 seconds after creation**, with about **2.154 MB** downloaded.
- Newly created workers also opened paired connections about **0.6–1.6 seconds after startup**, with individual observed responses of roughly 1–2 MB in the sampled examples.

These were connections to chatgpt.com. TLS was not decrypted, so their exact response bodies were not read.

#### Relevant implementation observations from the installed 0.8.92 bundle

Before uninstall, read-only source inspection found:

- `meetings_mcp.py` startup calls `start_discovery_rollout_lookup()` and `start_required_update_polling(...)`.
- `meetings_client_policy.py` defines a **600-second** policy refresh interval and a polling loop that can run without visible Meetings UI.
- There is a skip path when a native policy owner is available; we are **not** claiming every worker downloads the same amount on every interval.
- The policy/bootstrap implementation references `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/statsig/bootstrap`.
- The Node launcher starts a separate Python MCP service for each invocation.

The timing of the established worker's approximately 606-second repeat is consistent with this code. **Independent bootstrap/policy refresh across multiple workers is a hypothesis, not a decoded per-request attribution or a confirmed root cause.**

#### User uninstall and follow-up observation

The user manually uninstalled Meetings around **23:24**. Independent readback showed:

- Meetings was absent from the installed-plugin list and its former cache directory was absent.
- The 27 workers reduced to one, then the last worker exited by the **23:25:42** check.
- No process termination signal was sent by the diagnostic assistant.
- The original Codex app-server/desktop host and all 16 baseline Google Drive processes remained running; the proxy configuration hash was unchanged.

A second approximately four-minute sample at **23:24:57–23:28:59** used the same polling logic and captured **no Python-runtime traffic**. The last old worker exited during the first minute; this is not a guarantee of permanent zero traffic. Captured connections represented **99.152%** of the whole-machine transfer counter.

For transparency, whole-machine downloads changed from **105.898 MB to 44.004 MB**, but uploads increased from **9.458 MB to 131.021 MB**, and total transfer increased from **115.356 MB to 175.025 MB**. Concurrent Codex work, Drive synchronization, and an approximately 28.152 MB OpenAI component download changed the workload. Therefore this is **not a controlled benchmark or a claim that uninstall reduced total traffic**. The narrower observation is that the identified Meetings workers and their observed background downloads disappeared.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence, not a guaranteed minimal reproducer:

1. Use the macOS desktop app for ordinary non-Meetings work with Meetings 0.8.92 installed.
2. Without intentionally starting Meetings recording or meeting tools, inspect the Meetings MCP process chains and read-only per-process network counters.
3. Observe multiple workers and sample existing workers long enough to include a roughly ten-minute refresh boundary.
4. Compare worker existence and network activity after a user-directed uninstall, without restarting the desktop app or interrupting other work.

The exact trigger for accumulating 24–27 workers is not established. We did not reinstall the plugin or deliberately restart/stop other tasks to provoke it.

### What is the expected behavior?

Unused Meetings functionality should have bounded, modest background network usage. If multiple per-conversation MCP workers are expected, shared bootstrap/policy data should ideally avoid redundant large transfers, and worker lifecycle should not retain unnecessary instances.

Please clarify:

1. What triggers each worker's creation and retirement, and what idle instance count is expected?
2. Can policy/bootstrap responses be shared, cached, reduced or conditionally fetched across workers?
3. Is this consistent with a known 0.8.92 macOS issue, and is there a confirmed fixed version?
4. What credential-free endpoint/status/size/retry diagnostics would help investigate further?

### Additional information and privacy

Possibly related reports: #53588 (Windows 0.8.77 background network usage) and #52803 (Windows 0.8.77 multi-instance CPU usage). Different platforms/versions and potentially different causes; this report does not assert they share a root cause.

**Only this manually prepared, sanitized text summary is submitted. No attachments, raw logs, diagnostic bundles, session transcripts, meeting/recording content, document contents, screenshots, credentials, cookies, tokens, account details, private project names/paths, proxy/server IP addresses, device identifiers or actual PIDs are included.** No reproduction was attempted that would interrupt other active tasks.

labels.name: app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Codex Desktop: 26.1013.3656.0  Bundled Codex CLI: 0.163.0-alpha.10.2  Windows package: OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0  Platform: Windows x64

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT subscription: Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64

### What issue are you seeing?

A custom, OAuth-protected Streamable HTTP MCP connector cannot complete authentication through Codex Desktop.

The OAuth flow reaches the external browser, authenticates through Auth0, and redirects back to Codex Desktop. Chrome displays an "Open ChatGPT?" prompt for the codex://connector/oauth_callback handler.

After accepting the prompt, Codex Desktop opens and displays:

OAuth authorization response issuer does not match the expected issuer

The error is reproducible.

The MCP server's protected-resource metadata and Auth0 authorization-server metadata advertise exactly the same authorization-server issuer, including the trailing slash.

There is no evidence of a mismatch between those public discovery documents.

MCP server and OAuth configuration

MCP endpoint:

https://research-lfs-bridge-staging-staging.up.railway.app/mcp

Protected-resource metadata:

{
  "resource": "https://research-lfs-bridge-staging-staging.up.railway.app",
  "authorization_servers": [
    "https://dev-4duds3htsftf073l.us.auth0.com/"
  ],
  "scopes_supported": ["lfs:write"]
}

Authorization-server metadata:

URL:
https://dev-4duds3htsftf073l.us.auth0.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server

issuer:
https://dev-4duds3htsftf073l.us.auth0.com/

authorization_endpoint:
https://dev-4duds3htsftf073l.us.auth0.com/authorize

token_endpoint:
https://dev-4duds3htsftf073l.us.auth0.com/oauth/token

authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported:
true

code_challenge_methods_supported:
["S256", "plain"]

The Auth0 issuer in both documents is byte-for-byte identical.

The resource URL is intentionally different from the authorization-server issuer.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Steps to reproduce

Open the Windows Codex/ChatGPT Desktop application, version 26.1013.3656.0.

Use the custom Research LFS Bridge — Staging OAuth Test MCP connection.

Request a read-only call to the MCP status tool.

When authentication is required, initiate the normal OAuth authorization flow.

Complete authentication through Auth0 in Chrome.

Chrome displays an external-protocol confirmation, "Open ChatGPT?", associated with codex://connector/oauth_callback.

Accept the confirmation to return to Codex Desktop.

Observe the issuer-mismatch error.

This occurs without attempting uploads, repository writes, or configuration changes.

Actual behavior

Codex Desktop rejects the OAuth callback with:

OAuth authorization response issuer does not match the expected issuer

The expected and received issuer values are not shown in the error.

A Chrome console entry confirms that an external codex://connector/oauth_callback handler was launched. An iss parameter is visible in the redirect, beginning with the Auth0 tenant issuer, but its complete decoded value was not independently captured.

The precise value expected internally by Codex is therefore unknown.

### What is the expected behavior?

Expected behavior

Codex should:

Resolve the authorization-server issuer from the MCP protected-resource metadata's authorization_servers entry.

Preserve and compare that issuer exactly against the authorization-server metadata and RFC 9207 authorization-response iss parameter.

Complete the OAuth authorization flow when the validated values match.

Allow the authenticated, read-only MCP status call to execute.

Strict issuer validation must remain enabled.

### Additional information

Additional diagnostic evidence

The staging Railway service reports a successful deployment and previously served authenticated MCP requests.

No staging MCP HTTP request was recorded during the October 18 failed authorization attempt, consistent with the connection failing before the MCP tool call.

The existing production Research LFS Bridge MCP connection works in ChatGPT through a separate OAuth connection.

Local Codex configuration does not contain a Research LFS Bridge MCP server entry.

The current SQLite diagnostic database at ~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite records desktop activity during the failed authorization window, but does not contain the exact issuer-mismatch message or the expected/received issuer pair.

Four keyword-matched diagnostic entries during that window originated from the feedback_tags module, not an identified OAuth issuer-validation component.

No issuer-validation bypass, local patch, rollback, or alternate OAuth issuer configuration was attempted.

Possibly related issues

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/40885 — Expected issuer incorrectly derived from MCP resource URL rather than authorization_servers.

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37373 — Trailing-slash normalization of expected OAuth issuer in a previous app-server version.

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/31573 — Earlier RFC 9207 authorization-response issuer handling.

The present reproduction differs in that the browser authorization flow reaches the Codex Desktop callback before the error is displayed, and it occurs with bundled Codex CLI 0.163.0-alpha.10.2 on Windows.

Request

Please investigate the issuer value stored or expected by the Windows Codex Desktop OAuth callback handler in this version.

In particular, could the client be:

deriving the expected issuer from the MCP resource URL rather than authorization_servers;

normalizing away the trailing slash from the Auth0 issuer; or

losing/misinterpreting the RFC 9207 iss value during desktop callback handling?

If feasible, include the sanitized expected and received issuer identifiers in the diagnostic error, without exposing authorization codes, state values or tokens.

The requested fix should preserve strict OAuth issuer validation.
