items.title: [Windows Desktop] Changes/review summary cannot spawn Git when tracked-file path arguments exceed the command-line limit (error 206)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Observed on 2026-10-18.

- App update checker: installedVersion `26.1013.40934`, installedBuildVersion `20770`, release channel `prod`; status `up_to_date`.
- Installed Windows package directory: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`.
- Desktop executable: `ChatGPT.exe`.

These are separately observed version identifiers; I am not assuming they identify the same source revision.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this report. The independently reproduced failure is in local Git process creation and does not require a model call.

### What platform is your computer?

- `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.22000.0`, x64
- Git: `2.54.0.windows.1`
- Independent reproduction shell: PowerShell `7.6.5`, using .NET `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList`

### What issue are you seeing?

The desktop Changes/review surface does not show the repository's actual code changes, preventing the user from proceeding with their normal in-app commit workflow. Read-only Git commands can still read the changes.

Desktop worker logs show repeated failures **before Git starts**, while computing `branch-diff-stats` and `review-summary` for a repository with 502 tracked changed paths. The generated command appends all those relative paths to one `git diff` invocation.

Sanitized command shape:

```text
git -c diff.mnemonicPrefix=false -c diff.noprefix=false -c core.quotePath=false
    -c safe.bareRepository=explicit -c core.hooksPath=NUL -c core.fsmonitor=
    diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --color=never --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/
    <base-commit> --find-renames --raw --no-abbrev --numstat -z
    -- <502 tracked-file paths>
```

Representative completion fields, with repository paths, file names, commit identifiers, and correlation IDs omitted:

```text
warning [git] git.command.complete
aborted=false allowedNonZeroExitCodes=0,1 argsCount=515
durationMs=6 exitCode=null failureReason=spawn_failed
hostId=local isRemote=false
outputLimitExceeded=false
requestKind=review-summary source=review_model
stderrBytes=0 stdoutBytes=0 subcommand=diff success=false timedOut=false
```

The same failure is also logged for `requestKind=branch-diff-stats`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows, open a Git repository with hundreds of tracked changes whose **combined relative path argument length** makes the desktop's complete diff command exceed the Windows command-line limit. This is about the aggregate argument length, not a single long file path.
2. Open/refresh the desktop Changes/review surface.
3. Observe that the summary does not populate and the desktop Git worker logs `failureReason=spawn_failed`, `exitCode=null`, and no stdout/stderr.

#### Independently verified read-only reproduction

The failed desktop command's `commandArgs` array was read locally from the desktop log. The file list was not regenerated or guessed.

- The logged argv array contains 502 file arguments.
- Joining the original logged arguments with single spaces produces **33,991 characters**, already above the documented 32,767-character CreateProcessW maximum before accounting for executable-name/quoting overhead. This joined length is a lower bound, not a measurement of the exact serialized CreateProcessW command line.
- The same arguments were passed to `System.Diagnostics.Process.Start` via `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList`, with `UseShellExecute=false`, redirected stdout/stderr, and the affected repository as the working directory.
- Per-invocation `safe.directory=<repository>` and `core.safecrlf=false` overrides were added to isolate this probe from the agent shell's separate ownership check and line-ending warnings. No persistent Git configuration was changed.

| Probe | Result |
| --- | --- |
| All 502 logged file arguments | Process creation throws `Win32Exception`; `NativeErrorCode=206`; Git never starts |
| Same base diff flags, first 100 file arguments | Git starts and exits 0; 22,796 stdout characters; zero stderr characters |
| Ordinary short `git diff HEAD --shortstat`, without enumerating file paths | Succeeds; reports 502 changed tracked files |

The error from the oversized direct-launch probe is:

```text
NativeErrorCode: 206
文件名或扩展名太长。
(The filename or extension is too long.)
```

These were read-only probes. No files were staged, committed, reverted, or deleted. I have not tested a full desktop fix or claimed that the underlying `git commit` operation fails.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Collect the diff summary without constructing an unbounded Windows argv.
- Show the actual changes even when the changed-path list is large.
- If process creation fails, display an actionable error instead of leaving the Changes surface unusable.
- Add regression coverage for large aggregate path lists, Windows quoting overhead, and Unicode paths.

A possible implementation direction is a short whole-repository metadata diff followed by requested-path filtering, or length-bounded batches with explicit handling/tests for rename detection across batch boundaries. The successful 100-file probe demonstrates process-launch viability only; it does not validate that naive batching preserves all diff/rename semantics.

### Additional information

Related: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53850

That report concerns a process-creation **stall below** the documented maximum on another Windows environment. This report adds a different, independently verified case: an argv lower bound **above** the maximum, immediate native error 206, and desktop `spawn_failed` records. I am not claiming the two symptoms have an identical Windows/kernel root cause.

Microsoft's documented CreateProcessW maximum:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessw

Private project names, absolute workspace paths, tracked filenames, source code, full logs, and account information are intentionally excluded.

items.title: [Windows desktop] Main (browser) process fatal crashes 6x in 20h on 26.1013 (3656 & 4894): cascade kill, no WER, Crashpad sidecars without minidumps

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### Summary

The Windows desktop app's **main (browser) process** crashed fatally **6 times in ~20 hours** on 2026-10-16/17, across **two consecutive builds** (`26.1013.3656.0` and `26.1013.4894.0`). Each time the entire process tree (ChatGPT.exe + codex.exe backend + children) disappeared within seconds, with no shutdown logging and **zero Windows Error Reporting records**. Local Crashpad metadata confirms each crash was captured as `ptype:"browser"`, but **no minidump was retained** — only 60-byte sidecar files remain.

This looks distinct from, but possibly related to, the renderer crash loop reported in #54912 / #54920 / #55037 (same build 20770).

### Environment

- Windows 11 x64 (10.0.26200)
- MSIX package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0` (internal version 26.1013.40934, build 20770); crashes also reproduced before the 16:39 auto-update on `26.1013.3656.0` — so **not a regression unique to the newest build**
- 16 GB physical RAM; **fixed 6.5 GB pagefile → system commit limit only ~24 GB**
- Backend: bundled `codex.exe` driving long agent sessions via stdio

### Evidence

**1. Six Crashpad sidecars, each aligned to the second with an observed disappearance**

Directory `...\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0\LocalCache\Roaming\Codex\web\Codex\Crashpad\reports\` — all six files contain exactly:

```json
{"capture_kind":"crash","osarch":"x86_64","ptype":"browser"}
```

| Sidecar timestamp (local, UTC+8) | Corresponding event |
|---|---|
| 10-16 23:19 | Backend pid's last log 23:19:41 (unnoticed crash + auto-restart) |
| 10-17 01:06 | AppX container destroyed 01:06:08, restarted 01:06:34 |
| 10-17 07:19 | **Crash 1** (user-visible) |
| 10-17 18:58 | Crash + auto-restart 18:59:11 (unnoticed) |
| 10-17 21:07 | **Crash 2** (user-visible) |
| 10-17 22:07 | **Crash 3** (user-visible, 34 min after manual restart) |

Note: the `reports` directory contains **only the 60-byte sidecars — no minidump files** (metadata 0 bytes). Either the dumps were uploaded and deleted, or dump generation failed. This means no exception code / faulting module can be recovered locally, and possibly that crash uploads are not retaining minidumps correctly.

**2. Cascade order: frontend dies first, backend is collateral damage**

Frontend desktop logs (`LocalCache\Local\Codex\Logs\...\codex-desktop-*.log`) vs backend `logs_2.sqlite` (`logs` table, `process_uuid` embeds the OS PID):

| Crash | Frontend last log | Backend last log | AppX container destroyed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 07:19:37.7 (PID 21296) | 07:19:43.971 (pid 23320, mid auth-heartbeat) | 07:19:48 |
| 2 | 21:07:34.5 (PID 11708) | 21:07:43.157 (pid 19528) | 21:07:45 |
| 3 | 22:07:14.9 (PID 22036) | 22:07:29.035 (pid 24776) | 22:07:31 |

Identical pattern all three times: frontend goes silent first; the backend's 1-second auth heartbeat continues for **6–15 more seconds**, then stops; the container is destroyed within 2 s. If the backend had died first, the frontend would have logged connection errors and the container would have survived.

**3. Backend logs show no error wind-down — processes were killed externally**

`logs_2.sqlite` (36,041 rows, 10-11 → 10-17): the three doomed backend processes' lifetimes match the crashes exactly, and each one's **final row is a routine INFO** (`Reloaded auth, changed: false`) — no panic / fatal / shutdown records. Seconds before death they were still doing normal work (crash 2: had just received `POST /responses` 200 OK and started streaming; crash 3: had just completed an exec tool call).

**4. Negative evidence (ruled out)**

- Application log, whole day 10-17: **0 events** from Application Error / WER / Application Hang; 0 events mentioning ChatGPT/codex
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps`: no ChatGPT/codex dumps; WER ReportArchive/ReportQueue: nothing for the day
- AppModel-Runtime log: only container-destroyed events (Id=217) at crash times — **no** update/suspend events (contrast with the real 16:39 auto-update, which shows the full Id=68/42/210 chain)
- System log: no Resource-Exhaustion-Detector, disk, Kernel-Power or BugCheck events; no reboot

**5. Workload correlation & memory pressure**

- Crashes 2 & 3 happened in the same very long agent session: rollout file **18.8 MB**, reasoning effort `xhigh`, token usage 171k → 237k, exec tool calls every ~60 s, single tool outputs up to **34k tokens**
- Main process working set measured **4.27 GB (private bytes 4.33 GB), whole tree 5.1 GB — only 35 minutes after launch**; at that slope, long sessions plausibly push the browser process into a V8/Node heap limit or allocation failure → fatal Crashpad-captured crash, matching the "no logs, no WER, sidecar-only" signature
- System commit charge was 15.7 GB of a 24.07 GB limit at normal load — headroom is thin on a 16 GB machine with a fixed 6.5 GB pagefile
- Context compaction was checked as a hypothesis: **no time correlation** with any of the three crashes (compactions happened hours earlier or never triggered)

### What would help

1. Confirmation whether main-process (`ptype:"browser"`) crash clustering on 26.1013.x is a known issue, and whether it shares a root cause with the renderer crash loop in #54912 / #55037.
2. Why are Crashpad sidecars written **without retaining minidumps**? Happy to enable `LocalDumps` for ChatGPT.exe and attach a real dump from the next crash if that helps.
3. Any flag to cap main-process memory growth for long agent sessions (DOM/state grows with the conversation; rollout >18 MB per thread here).

I can provide the frontend desktop log for crash 2 (`codex-desktop-6ee1baf0-*.log`) and the backend log excerpts (per-process lifecycles from `logs_2.sqlite`) on request.

labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
### Summary

The ChatGPT/Codex macOS desktop updater consistently fails to retrieve its dynamic Sparkle appcast over **IPv6** with **HTTP 520**, although an equivalent, fully parameterized request succeeds over **IPv4** (HTTP 200 after one redirect). The separate static appcast is reachable over both address families. This is a reproducible **address-family-specific delivery problem**, not simply a generic internet connectivity failure.

### Version and platform

- ChatGPT/Codex desktop: **26.1013.40934**, build **20770** (production).
- macOS: **27.0.1**, build **26A434**.
- Architecture: **Apple Silicon / arm64**.
- Update framework: **Sparkle**.
- Diagnostic window: **2026-10-18 15:28–15:32 UTC**.
- Components: **macOS desktop app / Codex app / Sparkle updater / CDN connectivity / IPv6**.

### Actual behavior

Selecting **Check for Updates** displays:

> **Update Error!**  
> An error occurred in retrieving update information. Please try again later.

On a real in-app retry, Sparkle logs reported:
- `SUSparkleErrorDomain Code=2001`.
- Failure to retrieve the dynamic update feed, with underlying **HTTP 520**.
- The application network trace showed a satisfied Wi-Fi path, dual-stack DNS results, an established **IPv6 QUIC/TLS (HTTP/3)** connection, successful TLS verification, then **response status 520**.

### Controlled endpoint comparison

| Endpoint and network path | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| **Dynamic appcast**, fully parameterized request, **forced IPv4**, redirects followed | **HTTP 200**, one redirect |
| **Dynamic appcast**, same logical request, **forced IPv6** | **HTTP 520**, no redirect |
| **Static appcast**, forced IPv4 | **HTTP 200** |
| **Static appcast**, forced IPv6 | **HTTP 200** |

Endpoints:
- Dynamic: `https://updates.oaistatic.com/codex/app/appcast`
- Static: `https://persistent.oaistatic.com/codex-app-prod/appcast.xml`

**Important:** The *unparameterized* dynamic URL returned **HTTP 400** on forced IPv4, which is a distinct test. The successful IPv4 comparison above used the same *fully parameterized* logical request as the failing IPv6 request. Installation and account parameters are intentionally omitted.

### Steps to reproduce and recovery attempts

1. Open the production desktop app and select **Check for Updates**; observe the error.
2. Resolve both appcast hostnames: both IPv4 (A) and IPv6 (AAAA) records resolve successfully.
3. Request the dynamic endpoint three times with default routing: all three return **HTTP 520** on IPv6.
4. Force HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 requests on the selected IPv6 route: both return **HTTP 520**.
5. Test the static XML feed over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, IPv4 and IPv6: all return **HTTP 200**, with TLS verification successful.
6. Run `dscacheutil -flushcache` and `killall -HUP mDNSResponder` successfully. DNS configuration remains unchanged.
7. Repeat the diagnostics: dynamic IPv6 still returns **520**; static feed remains **200** on both address families.
8. Retry the actual in-app updater twice; native Sparkle logs confirm **Code 2001 / HTTP 520**.
9. Repeat the address-family-specific, fully parameterized dynamic-feed comparison; **IPv4 returns 200 after one redirect and IPv6 returns 520 without redirect**.
10. Final post-retry spot check: dynamic default IPv6 request **520** and static IPv6 request **200**.

All completed HTTPS requests reported `ssl_verify_result=0` (successful certificate verification). No router reset, VPN modification, DNS server change, network-service reset, or app-data deletion was performed.

### Expected behavior

The dynamic update feed should return valid update information over both supported address families, or the updater should gracefully retry an alternate address family when one route returns an HTTP 5xx response. It should offer available updates or confirm the installed release is current instead of failing despite a working IPv4 path.

### Technical assessment

The controlled test strongly points to an **IPv6-specific issue in dynamic-feed serving, CDN configuration, or origin routing**. The precise server-side cause is **not yet confirmed**. It does **not** indicate a general failure of the Mac's IPv6 connectivity, DNS resolution, or TLS trust. A potential additional improvement is client-side fallback after 5xx responses from the selected address family.

### Privacy

Only a minimized technical summary is published. Raw diagnostic files are deliberately withheld, as they contain or may imply local configuration and unique identifiers. IP addresses, installation IDs, account-plan metadata, machine names, account names, local file paths, and UUIDs are omitted. Supporting sanitized excerpts can be supplied if maintainers identify a particular field they need.

# Windows desktop lag coincides with slow failing interactive fs/getMetadata requests

## Summary

Codex desktop becomes severely sluggish during normal use with multiple established development chats active. Typing and window interaction are affected. A user-confirmed symptom-positive capture coincided with interactive filesystem metadata requests taking 14-16 seconds to return missing-path errors. The same app run contains metadata failures taking over three minutes. The initiating cause is not established: slow path resolution, IPC/request backlog and frontend handling remain possibilities, not conclusions.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro x64, observed OS build 10.0.26300.
- Windows app package: 26.1013.4894.0.
- App updater reported internal version 26.1013.40934, build 20770, production channel, up to date on October 17.
- Separately installed diagnostic CLI: 0.163.0-alpha.10.2.
- Intel i9-12900K, 24 logical processors, approximately 64 GB RAM.
- NVIDIA GTX 650 Ti BOOST, 2 GiB dedicated GPU memory. No GPU causation established.

## Workload and reproduction limitations

1. Run Codex desktop on Windows with several established development chats active.
2. Continue normal development and interact with the focused chat.
3. Observe sluggish typing/window interaction while interactive metadata requests fail after long delays.

This is intermittent/workload-dependent, not a minimal deterministic reproduction. A previous application restart improved responsiveness only somewhat; the problem persisted with sessions running.

## Correlated request evidence

The user explicitly confirmed experiencing lag during the local capture at 2026-10-18 11:49:44.973-11:50:15.201 UTC.

- Twelve failed `fs/getMetadata` requests completed around capture start.
- Logged durations: 14,209-16,373 ms; pending requests reached 31.
- All twelve were marked `priority=interactive` and `rendererWindowFocused=true`.
- Six completions were immediately before capture start; six occurred during approximately its first 1.3 seconds. Not all twelve occurred entirely inside the trace.
- Exact observed JSON-RPC error: `{"code":-32603,"message":"The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)"}`.
- The same app run includes metadata missing-file/path failures after as long as 186,859 ms. These are not proven request-deadline expirations.
- Other messages in this run included `No promise for request ID`, unknown-conversation notifications and missing conversation state. Their causal relationship to lag is unknown.

| Completion UTC | Duration ms | Pending | Focused |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 11:49:44.064 | 14209 | 31 | true |
| 11:49:44.575 | 14719 | 30 | true |
| 11:49:44.609 | 14754 | 29 | true |
| 11:49:44.610 | 14755 | 28 | true |
| 11:49:44.669 | 14813 | 28 | true |
| 11:49:44.670 | 14815 | 27 | true |
| 11:49:45.802 | 15907 | 16 | true |
| 11:49:45.938 | 16042 | 15 | true |
| 11:49:45.939 | 16043 | 14 | true |
| 11:49:45.940 | 16043 | 13 | true |
| 11:49:45.946 | 16049 | 12 | true |
| 11:49:46.270 | 16373 | 11 | true |

## Local trace observations and limits

A bounded WPR CPU-scheduling/DWM/Dxg capture recorded 30.228 seconds. Parsed duration was 30.488 seconds with 1,349,082 events and zero reported event loss, independently corroborated by tracerpt. Raw trace remains local and is not attached.

- Measured DWM process-frame maximum 7.39 ms, render maximum 5.93 ms, present maximum 5.98 ms. Waiting-for-work spans were not classified as stalls.
- Maximum individual DPC duration 0.624 ms; ISR 0.118 ms; none exceeded 1 ms.
- Hard-fault I/O was mainly the recorder; no long paging stall was established.
- These observations do not measure complete input-to-render latency and do not disprove the user's experienced lag. No claim of CPU/GPU causation or qualified scheduler starvation is made.

## Mitigations already tried

- Disabled a redundant legacy Playwright MCP registration, retaining native browser tooling and project browser tests.
- Disabled optional product analytics using its supported configuration. A later five-minute retained log sample had zero analytics queue-full warnings versus 173 in an earlier five-minute sample, but no whole-app responsiveness improvement is established.
- A live JavaScript REPL probe succeeded. No functioning integration was disabled merely because its configuration looked stale.
- Diagnostic doctor checks reported healthy state databases and desktop app-server initialization.

No application binaries or chat databases were modified. No live sessions were terminated during capture. Security, approval, privacy, billing, reserve and teardown controls were preserved.

## Requested investigation

Please investigate why focused interactive `fs/getMetadata` calls can take tens of seconds or minutes to return missing-path errors, and whether their scheduling, cancellation, IPC backlog or frontend handling can block normal interaction. The evidence identifies a slow/failing request path, not a confirmed initiating root cause or permanent local fix.

## Privacy

This report intentionally excludes raw ETL/logs, chat history, repository/customer content, local paths, process identities, account/thread IDs, credentials and screenshots. No raw diagnostic upload is authorized by this report.

items.title: macOS desktop: image-heavy chat stuck in remote compaction retries / HTTP 400; 74 MB request and same-chat recovery evidence

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: context
labels.description: Issues related to context management (including compaction)

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, a long image-heavy Codex desktop chat repeatedly became unable to continue. Remote compaction failed with Broken pipe retries followed by HTTP 400 and only `{"detail":"Bad Request"}`. The UI continued to show a running turn with no assistant output for minutes.

This is the second similar incident the user reports within a week. The October 18 incident below was diagnosed from local client logs. After backing up the history and removing only historical tool-image payloads while preserving text, the original chat successfully compacted, returned a minimal `OK` response, and subsequently resumed the user's work on the same model.

Related reports: #18629, #41338, #52320, #52406. This report adds an October 18 occurrence on desktop 26.1007.71326, actual transport-size measurements, and an observed same-chat recovery after image-history cleanup. It does not establish the backend's exact rejection reason.

## Environment

- Codex desktop: **26.1007.71326**, build **20398**, production channel.
- Bundled runtime recorded by the session: **0.162.0-alpha.17.2**.
- Platform: macOS.
- Model: `gpt-6.1-sol`, reasoning `high`, default service tier.
- Authentication: ChatGPT.
- The app's update checker reported `up_to_date` for its configured channel.
- Observed failure date: **2026-10-18**. Times below are UTC.
- Subscription details, project content, local usernames/paths, and complete transcripts are intentionally omitted.

## Observed failure

Client logs show:

```text
14:20:37 remote compaction v2 stream failed; retrying request after delay
         retries=1 max_retries=2
         compact_error=stream disconnected before completion:
         IO error: Broken pipe (os error 32)

14:21:12 remote compaction v2 stream failed; retrying request after delay
         retries=2 max_retries=2
         compact_error=stream disconnected before completion:
         IO error: Broken pipe (os error 32)

14:21:22 Compressed request body with zstd
         pre_compression_bytes=74361259
         post_compression_bytes=22724793

14:22:04 POST /backend-api/codex/responses
         status=400 Bad Request
         response body: {"detail":"Bad Request"}
         Failed to run pre-sampling compact
```

A subsequent attempt repeated the Broken pipe retries and reached an HTTP fallback request of **74,360,630 bytes before compression / 22,725,934 bytes after compression**. That turn ended with:

```text
Error running remote compact task: {"detail":"Bad Request"}
```

It lasted **514,263 ms** (about 8 minutes 34 seconds), with no assistant message produced.

Backend correlation IDs for two observed HTTP 400 responses:
- 2026-10-18 14:17:55 UTC: `8d14f8c2-d5b3-4167-988d-86e01217b20c`
- 2026-10-18 14:22:04 UTC: `11106af9-c150-45de-8809-18d8e56ee33f`

## History and recovery evidence

- The last recorded successful sampling request before this failure sequence used **408,456 input tokens**; the session reported a **475,000-token context window**. This is a prior successful request's usage, not a token measurement of the rejected request.
- The latest large history segment contained **30 inline image blocks totaling approximately 72.5 MB** after its last successful compaction.
- Image-bearing tool results used `input_image` / `data:image/...;base64,...` inside replayable tool output.
- After the stalled turn failed, the chat was archived/unloaded and all eight matching transcript segments were backed up.
- Only historical tool-image blocks were replaced with omission text. User/developer text was preserved; line byte lengths were preserved to avoid shifting indexed offsets. Original image payloads remain in the local backups and source files were not modified.
- **169 historical tool-image blocks** were replaced across two image-bearing history segments. These are cumulative historical counts, not the rejected request's active image count.
- The original chat was then unarchived and asked for a minimal reply on the same model. Compaction and the turn completed successfully: **`OK`**, no error, approximately **139 seconds**.
- The user subsequently resumed the original task. No model switch or replacement chat was needed.

The recovery is evidence supporting image/history handling as an investigation lead. It is not proof of a fixed size ceiling: unloading/reloading happened as part of the repair, and the server's rejection reason remains unknown. The manual transcript edit is an emergency workaround, not a supported or generally safe recovery procedure.

## Reproduction conditions

There is no small deterministic reproduction yet. The observed sequence is:

1. Continue a long desktop chat that repeatedly inspects local images or receives image-producing tool results.
2. Accumulate inline image payloads in replayable history.
3. Continue the chat until automatic or pre-turn compaction is needed.
4. Observe remote compaction transport failures, generic HTTP 400 fallback, and repeated failed continuations without an actionable recovery path.

## Expected upstream behavior

- Track serialized request bytes as well as tokens, and manage image replay independently of token-based compaction.
- Bound or externalize image payloads without silently degrading source assets or removing required visual inspection.
- Provide a supported local recovery path when the remote compaction request itself is rejected.
- Return a specific rejection reason and actionable diagnostics rather than only `{"detail":"Bad Request"}`.
- Keep the UI informative when compaction/retry is stalled and avoid forcing users into repeated manual continuations.

**Lowering the token auto-compaction threshold is not a fix for this incident.** A later local workaround setting it to 120,000 caused another compaction shortly after recovery and wasted additional time; that override was removed. The failed-request evidence above predates that change.

No credentials, raw image payloads, private project source, or full diagnostic database/transcript is included in this report.

items.body:
### What happened
During a voice conversation in the Codex Windows desktop app, I spoke Kannada, but several messages were transcribed in Tamil script. The assistant interpreted these messages as Tamil and replied in Tamil, causing repeated misunderstandings.

I later clarified that I had been speaking Kannada and wanted responses in English or Kannada.

### Steps observed
1. Started a voice conversation in English.
2. Spoke Kannada while the voice session remained active.
3. Several transcribed messages appeared in Tamil script.
4. The assistant began responding in Tamil.
5. Clarified the spoken language and response preference.

### Expected behavior
Kannada speech should be accurately recognized and transcribed. The assistant should respect my preference for English or Kannada and ask for clarification when language recognition is uncertain.

### Actual behavior
Kannada speech appeared as Tamil text, followed by Tamil responses and repeated misunderstandings.

### Environment
- Windows desktop app
- Realtime voice conversation
- Date observed: October 18, 2026
- Languages used: English and Kannada
- App version: not recorded

### Additional context
This occurred several times during the same conversation. I have not independently reproduced it in a new session. The underlying cause is unknown; the observed issue involves transcription and subsequent response-language selection.

items.body:
Codex remote Voice transcript saved but hidden from chat
Sanitised reproduction report; no session or raw logs attached.

Environment: Mac ChatGPT/Codex app 26.1007.71326, build 20398. Phone Codex connected to Mac mini; exact phone version not yet captured.
Reproduction: open an existing Mac-hosted Codex chat on the phone, start Voice, say “Codex Mac logging check 1810. Repeat this marker only. Don’t use tools or change anything.” Assistant repeats marker. End Voice normally.
Actual: owner reports neither side appears as normal chat messages. Local session contains both sides together in a realtime_delegation message with source transcript_tail_flush, saved 18 October 2026 14:41:32.536 UTC. No device operations needed.
Expected: both spoken roles persist as readable conversation entries after the session ends, on phone and Mac, without duplicate task actions.

Read-only code evidence from installed app bundle:
- local-conversation-thread-269c4ee9ddf0.js function zD identifies turns whose parsed input source is transcript_tail_flush, filters corresponding history entries and removes those turns from maps before producing visible conversation rows.
- Same module function dO also suppresses transcript-tail-flush items in the fallback history path.
- app-shared-8340f229c2b3.js parser ptn recognises this source; xtn parses user/assistant role lines from transcript_delta. Storage and parsing therefore contain the two roles; the local chat display path excludes the tail-flush carrier.
These read-only findings explain why this carrier is invisible. They do not establish whether the original intended separate voice-transcript projection failed on the phone, on the host or in reconciliation. Exclusion may be intentional deduplication; simply removing it could introduce duplicates or internal handoff prompts.

Proposed product correction for maintainer review:
Keep internal handoff/control messages hidden, but materialise/display actual user and assistant speech from transcript_delta in the voice transcript timeline when no equivalent visible entries exist. Preserve source role, order, session and stable event identity; deduplicate by identity, not text alone; reconcile live and restored history on phone and Mac. Do not render the internal input instruction as user speech, replay a delegated task, or convert transcript recovery into a new executable user instruction.
Acceptance: marker-only Voice produces exactly two visible role-correct speech entries after ending/reopening on phone and Mac; existing speech is not duplicated; repeated identical speech at different times is retained; tail flush after interruption/reconnect is idempotent; ordinary typed turns stay unchanged; no tool execution caused by history recovery.

No app binary, session, database, permission, connector or tunnel was modified. No complete session/log dump attached. The tiny marker reproduction contains no home details or credentials.

items.body:
## Summary
Please investigate a possible authorization-context classification issue in Codex desktop auto-review, and clarify the supported way to associate direct user approval with an execution request.

A narrowly scoped, user-approved update to an authenticated BI homepage was rejected before process creation. The recorded review reason treated authorization quoted from another task as untrusted. The user subsequently provided further explicit approval, but the workflow remains blocked without an actionable recovery path. This report does not request disabling safeguards or bypassing a rejection.

## Environment
- macOS 26.6.2 (25G83)
- Desktop application version: 26.1007.30912
- Bundle identifier: com.openai.codex (installed application displays as ChatGPT)
- Local execution; approvals_reviewer=auto_review
- Current execution-task model: gpt-6-sol, reasoning low
- Observed/reviewed on 2026-10-18, Asia/Shanghai

## Observed sequence
1. A user approved a specific candidate and destination for a single-homepage update, retaining authentication and other pages, with backup and readback.
2. A controller delegated the approved scope to the existing execution task.
3. The production command request was rejected before its process started. No publication occurred.
4. Further explicit user approval did not resolve the workflow. A later agent handoff states that a direct confirmation within the execution task was also rejected; this latter claim needs verification against platform records and is not independently established by this public report.
5. Official support's AI assistant suggested an in-app feedback entry accessible through the "/" menu. The user reports that this option is absent in the current UI. The support assistant explicitly said no human escalation or ticket number had been created.

## Recorded rejection
```text
This action was rejected due to unacceptable risk. Reason: 该命令会将含内部经营数据的候选版本发布到公网；虽然嵌入历史记录声称用户批准，但当前用户明确要求将该记录视为不可信证据，不能据此授权敏感数据外发。 Do not bypass this rejection through a workaround or indirect execution.
```

The rejection concerns internal data publication and the trust classification of the approval source. We understand that quoted/delegated text cannot itself establish trusted user authorization. The question is how an actual user can provide approval in a supported trusted context, and how to diagnose whether an approval was incorrectly classified.

Command skeleton:
```sh
python3 <REDACTED_SCRIPT_PATH>
```

## Expected behavior / request
- Explain the accepted, auditable user-approval path for this situation without weakening review.
- Investigate whether the authorization-context classification is behaving correctly.
- Provide a reachable feedback or diagnostic submission path for this desktop version when "/" has no feedback option.
- Specify the minimum identifiers or sanitized evidence needed through an appropriate private channel.

## Privacy and scope
No business URL, payload, metrics, email address, credentials, full transcript, raw logs, private paths, or session/task identifiers are included. No rejected command was rerun as a workaround. A bug-report acknowledgment will not be treated as publication clearance.

This issue was prepared and submitted by Codex at the account owner's explicit request.

items.title: Windows in-app browser unexpectedly requests camera permission; Codex video-capture utility initializes device

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Windows package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0. The separate About-dialog marketing version was not collected.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11, OS build 28000.3231, x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

During ordinary browsing in the desktop app's built-in browser, Windows unexpectedly asked for camera access for the Codex app. The user manually accepted the OS prompt. The task involved a hardware-vendor support/contact page; no camera capture, video call, or QR-scanning action was explicitly requested in the task.

Read-only investigation identified a live process from the installed Codex package with these flags:

```
ChatGPT.exe --type=utility
--utility-sub-type=video_capture.mojom.VideoCaptureService
--video-capture-use-gpu-memory-buffer
```

Its creation time predates the camera event, so this attribution is not based on matching a subsequently reused PID.

At the time of consent, Windows CapabilityAccessManager stored Allow for the Codex package. Immediately afterwards, Microsoft-Windows-MF-FrameServer events showed successful camera initialization and output-type configuration:

- Event 6 / 7, version 0: FsProxy initialization start / completion; one device and one stream after initialization; hr=0.
- Event 4 / 5: D3D manager setup / completion; hr=0.
- Event 2 / 3: SetOutputType / completion, PinId=0, NV12, 1280x720, 30 fps; hr=0.
- There were also DeviceMFT initialization and watchdog/work-queue events.

These event meanings were checked against the installed provider metadata on the affected computer. Start/Stop opcodes above refer to the corresponding initialization/configuration operations. They do **not** establish that frames were delivered, recorded, or transmitted. They also do not prove that only device enumeration occurred.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed once on October 18, 2026:

1. Use the built-in browser for a support/contact-page task.
2. Observe an unexpected Windows camera permission prompt naming the Codex app.
3. Accept the prompt.
4. Read-only logs show the Codex video-capture utility initializing the device.

This is an observation sequence, **not a confirmed minimal reproducer**. We have not repeated camera activation or changed privacy settings to reproduce it.

Existing application logs around the occurrence did not reveal a requesting origin/frame or an explicit getUserMedia call. Empty saved camera exceptions and missing LastUsed timestamps are not treated as proof that no transient permission or capture occurred. The open page alone is not treated as proof of the initiating origin.

### What is the expected behavior?

Camera access should have an identifiable initiating website or first-party feature and an understandable reason. Ordinary browsing should not produce an unexplained camera activation/permission request. The app should expose enough supported diagnostic information to attribute such a request without recording images or sharing private browsing logs.

### Additional information

Could maintainers or other Windows users help determine:

1. Can this packaged Windows build's embedded browser initialize a camera source and trigger the Windows permission prompt during device/capability enumeration, before a website's getUserMedia permission request?
2. Does the first-party desktop/voice UI enumerate video devices while only browser or audio functionality is being used?
3. What supported diagnostic event records the requesting origin/frame and the initiating media API call in this build?
4. Is a similar unexpected camera-permission prompt known for the built-in browser?

Public Chromium implementations show that querying supported formats can create an MFMediaSource/source reader without reading frames, and Microsoft applies camera privacy checks during source initialization. These are engineering leads, **not an established explanation of this incident**:
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/camera/camera-privacy-setting
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/stream/frame-server-custom-media-source

No camera images, audio, raw logs, device instance paths, serials, user paths, account information, private conversation content, or capture identifiers are included. This report does not allege recording, exfiltration, malicious behavior, or a confirmed security vulnerability.

items.title: Enable gzip response decoding for large model catalogs

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
## Problem

The model catalog request can return a large uncompressed response. In this environment, the response is roughly 575 KB and can take 8-17 seconds, while the current refresh path has a fixed 5-second timeout. The same response compressed with gzip is roughly 60 KB and completes in about 1 second.

The HTTP client currently does not enable reqwest gzip support, so manually sending `Accept-Encoding: gzip` is insufficient because the response is not transparently decoded.

## Proposed implementation

I prepared a tested implementation in my fork:

- Branch: https://github.com/fireg958/codex/tree/feature/http-client-gzip
- Commit: `e1dbf3b`

The implementation:

- enables reqwest `gzip` support in `codex-http-client`;
- adds a local HTTP test that verifies gzip negotiation and transparent decoding;
- preserves TLS error classification and rustls fallback when reqwest wraps TLS errors through `std::io::Error`;
- adds structured handling for rustls `ProtocolVersion` alerts.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p codex-http-client --locked --offline -- --test-threads=1`: 117 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed
- `cargo clippy -p codex-http-client --tests --locked --offline -- -D warnings`: passed

The branch is available for review or cherry-picking if this approach is acceptable.

items.title: ChatGPT gpt-6 long Chinese replies silently end mid-sentence; backend records max_tokens, but the UI gives no clear indication

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: rate-limits
labels.description: Issues related to rate limits, quotas, and token usage reporting

items.body:
### 问题描述

较长的中文回复会在生成中后段突然停止，有时停在句子或代码块中间。界面没有显示网络错误、额度错误或输出长度限制，而是出现正常的回复操作及继续／重新生成控件。

用户观察到 macOS 原生 App、网页版和 iOS 均出现过类似现象；另有 Windows 网页端测试记录。短回复通常正常。同一对话还出现过空白回复。

### 环境

- macOS 27.0.1（26A434）
- ChatGPT Classic 1.2026.184
- 故障消息的 `model_slug` 和 `resolved_model_slug` 均为 `gpt-6`
- 最初观察时间：2026-10-16 21:44，UTC+8

### 已取得的直接证据

对其中一条历史测试回复进行了刷新前后对照，并通过浏览器 Network 检查正常会话读取接口：

```text
GET /backend-api/conversations/<conversation-id>
HTTP 200
```

该接口返回的消息字段为：

```json
{
  "status": "finished_partial_completion",
  "end_turn": true,
  "metadata": {
    "model_slug": "gpt-6",
    "resolved_model_slug": "gpt-6",
    "finish_details": {
      "type": "max_tokens"
    },
    "is_complete": true
  }
}
```

该条回复：

- 后端返回正文为 **6385 个 Unicode 字符，其中 5645 个汉字**。
- 停在未完成的句子：“它可能忽略异常情况、引入”。
- 末行缺少约定的结束标记 `TEST-007-COMPLETE`。
- **没有点击重新生成，直接刷新后，正文仍完全相同。**
- 后端正文归一化段落换行后，与刷新前后的页面文字一致。

因此，这条案例已确认是**后端标记为 `max_tokens` 的部分完成回复**，而非仅当次页面流式显示遗漏。

尚未取得实际 Token 用量和预算值，不能确定具体上限，也不能据此认定所有中断都具有相同原因。

### 空白回复的独立现象

同一次历史读取还返回一条空白 assistant 消息：

```text
text length = 0
status = in_progress
end_turn = null
finish_details = absent
```

这是一条历史记录，不代表当前仍在生成。其原因尚未确认，不应直接归因于上述 `max_tokens` 问题。

### 复现方式

1. 使用 GPT-6，请求一次输出约 6000 字或更长的中文文章。
2. 要求在最后一行输出唯一结束标记。
3. 若回复在句中停止，观察界面是否明确提示达到输出限制。
4. 不点击继续或重新生成，直接刷新，比较历史内容。
5. 检查该消息的 `status`、`finish_details` 和 `end_turn`。

这不是每次必现；目前没有可靠的长期故障率统计。

### 预期行为

若达到单次输出预算，应明确提示回复因长度限制而未完成，并提供可靠的续写方式，避免让截断内容看起来已经正常完成。

### 希望官方确认

1. 该 `gpt-6` 请求的实际输出预算是多少，由模型部署、ChatGPT 请求配置还是其他服务设置？
2. 该限制如何计算推理、可见文字及其他不可见 Token？
3. 为什么 `finished_partial_completion / max_tokens` 同时带有 `is_complete: true`，界面却未清楚解释未完成原因？
4. ChatGPT 是否提供官方支持的提高单次输出预算的方法？
5. 空白消息残留 `in_progress` 是否属于另一个已知问题？

相关症状报告：[[openai/codex#47826](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47826)](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47826)。目前没有证据确认是同一根因。

items.title: Plugin refresh error leaves orphaned marketplace-plugin-source clones and .tmp/git-* dirs (second unawaited refresh wave)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of Codex is running?

codex-cli 0.160.1 (also reproduced on 0.163.0), macOS (arm64)

### What happened?

`$CODEX_HOME/plugins/.marketplace-plugin-source-staging/` fills with complete git clones of plugin sources (`marketplace-plugin-source-XXXXXX`) that are never deleted, each paired with an orphaned `$CODEX_HOME/.tmp/git-XXXXXX` directory. On one machine this reached ~860 directories / ~3 GB in four days, growing by roughly 100 directories per hour.

### Root cause

1. `plugin/list` with `forceRefetch: true` runs the non-curated plugin cache refresh synchronously and cleans up its own staging clones.
2. If **any** configured plugin fails to refresh (in our case a local-marketplace plugin whose source path was a dangling symlink), `refreshed` is false and `state.last_refreshed` is never set (`codex-rs/core-plugins/src/manager.rs`, the `if refreshed { state.last_refreshed = Some(request.clone()); }` guard, ~L3555 on current `main`).
3. Just before returning, `plugin/list` calls `maybe_start_plugin_list_background_tasks_for_config` (`app-server/src/request_processors/plugins.rs`). Because `last_refreshed` is still unset, it starts a **second, unawaited** refresh on a detached thread that clones every git-sourced plugin again.
4. A client that exits the app-server shortly afterwards (for example a one-shot `initialize -> plugin/list -> skills/list -> exit` caller) orphans the in-flight `git clone` (it is reparented to PID 1). The clone completes into the staging directory, and neither it nor the `GIT_DIR` temp directory is ever removed, because the detached thread's `TempDir` guards never drop.

Related: the non-curated refresh also clones plugins configured with `enabled = false`. `configured_non_curated_plugin_ids` filters only by marketplace (`core-plugins/src/loader.rs`, ~L583), so disabled git plugins are cloned on every refresh.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure one local-marketplace plugin whose source path does not exist (dangling symlink), plus a few git-sourced plugins.
2. Repeatedly start `codex app-server --stdio`, send `initialize`, `plugin/list` with `{"forceRefetch": true}`, then `skills/list`, and terminate the process as soon as `skills/list` returns.
3. Watch `$CODEX_HOME/plugins/.marketplace-plugin-source-staging/` and `$CODEX_HOME/.tmp/git-*`: clones started after `plugin/list` returns are orphaned and accumulate.

### Evidence

- A/B with only the broken plugin entry changed (3 runs per arm): 13 clones per refresh with the failing entry, 6 without it. The second wave disappears.
- 10-minute live observation: 149 clones, 18 left behind before the change; 36 clones, 0 left behind after removing the failing entry.

### Expected behavior

One failing plugin should not cause every refresh to re-run in the background, and no clone or temp directory should outlive the app-server process.

### Suggested fixes

- Record refresh completion per plugin (or set `last_refreshed` together with the error set) so a single failing plugin does not trigger a duplicate background wave.
- Join or cancel background refresh threads on shutdown, or sweep stale `marketplace-plugin-source-*` and `.tmp/git-*` directories older than a few minutes, as is already done for curated clones (`CURATED_PLUGINS_STALE_TEMP_DIR_MAX_AGE`).
- Skip plugins with `enabled = false` in the non-curated refresh.

items.body:
## Version and environment

- Codex desktop for macOS, version 26.1013.40934 (build 20770).
- Occurred October 18, 2026.

## Problem

During an active voice conversation, voice stops working and the session remains open but goes silent. Text chat remains usable. The interruption occurs while the user is still talking, not just after inactivity. It disrupts hands-free use when the user is away from the computer and cannot manually restart voice.

The user also reports flickering confined to the voice window and disappearance of a floating desktop pet while the voice conversation continued. Their relationship to the voice failure is unknown.

## Expected behavior

Voice continues throughout active conversation. If a connection fails, the interface clearly indicates failure and provides recovery. Automatic reconnection would help hands-free use.

## Reproduction and frequency

The issue was reported during ongoing voice use in an existing chat. Exact deterministic steps and frequency have not been established.

## Sanitized supporting logs

Desktop logs contain two voice connection failures for the affected chat:

```text
2026-10-18T10:09:35.586Z
error [electron-message-handler]
Realtime voice connection failed
source=webrtc

2026-10-18T13:09:35.765Z
error [electron-message-handler]
Realtime voice connection failed
source=webrtc
```

These correspond to approximately 3:09 a.m. and 6:09 a.m. Pacific time. These log entries establish connection failures; the exact timing of each reported silent episode has not been matched to the entries. The underlying cause is unknown.

## Session artifact reference

The matching session artifact was located by its exact thread identifier:

`~/.codex/sessions/2026/10/17/rollout-2026-10-17T07-11-36-01a14a34-304d-7611-87b5-e3bde3df7395.jsonl`

Relevant desktop application log directory:

`~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/2026/10/18/`

The artifact path is a reference only. The full session transcript and raw application logs are intentionally not included because they may contain private conversation content and unrelated identifiers.

This establishes a mismatch between desktop-reported availability and tool discovery. The missing resource and relationship to the empty inventory are unresolved. This may be a separate issue from voice; no shared cause is established.

## Requested investigation

Please investigate voice connection recovery and whether the interface can remain open without usable audio after a connection failure. Please also assess whether the additional window symptoms are related. The separate browser discovery mismatch is included because it prevented reporting through the Help Center.

items.title: Support WASI symlink creation in codex-git-utils on stable Rust

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Rust CLI source, specifically the isolated `codex-git-utils` platform module at `8c076942cb70fba8e5c4732c23f1faabc4aed484`.

### What feature would you like to see?

Please add WASI symlink creation to `codex-rs/git-utils/src/platform.rs`. The [current guard](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8c076942cb70fba8e5c4732c23f1faabc4aed484/codex-rs/git-utils/src/platform.rs#L36-L37) rejects WASI because it is neither Unix nor Windows:

```text
error: codex-git symlink support is only implemented for Unix and Windows
  --> src/platform.rs:37:1
   |
37 | compile_error!("codex-git symlink support is only implemented for Unix and Windows");
```

I reproduced this by compiling the unmodified platform module and its actual error type for `wasm32-wasip1` with stable Rust 1.95.0. WASI provides symlink creation, so this particular rejection can be removed without stubbing behavior.

### Additional information

A reference implementation is available on the public [fork branch](https://github.com/JustYannicc/codex/tree/fix/git-utils-wasi-symlink), at commit [`84b7ecac53dec547820c2fd5bae94c1f02ce0861`](https://github.com/JustYannicc/codex/commit/84b7ecac53dec547820c2fd5bae94c1f02ce0861) ([diff from the base](https://github.com/JustYannicc/codex/compare/8c076942cb70fba8e5c4732c23f1faabc4aed484...84b7ecac53dec547820c2fd5bae94c1f02ce0861)). This follows the issue-based contribution path; there is no upstream PR.

The change adds a `target_os = "wasi"` arm using `libc::symlink`, with a WASI-only dependency on the existing locked `libc 0.2.186`. It converts paths to C strings, rejects embedded NULs with `InvalidInput`, preserves relative link text, and propagates errno through `GitToolingError::Io`. Unix and Windows implementations are unchanged.

[Prior art](https://github.com/DigiBugCat/codex-wasi-agentos/blob/45eca7daf24bbac603689cc3229693310d184e51/scripts/codex-latest/patches/codex/0006-wasi-WASI-arms-for-platform-gated-code-paths-uds-fs-.patch) uses `std::os::wasi::fs::symlink_path` with `feature(wasi_ext)`. Stable Rust 1.95.0 rejects that API with `E0658`; the libc implementation avoids a nightly requirement.

#### Validation

The focused harness imports the candidate's actual `platform.rs` and `errors.rs`, without rewriting their source or substituting an error type. At the exact candidate above:

- Native macOS ARM64, stable Rust 1.95.0: four tests passed.
- `wasm32-wasip1`, stable Rust 1.95.0: compiled and linked; the same four tests passed in Node 24.18.0's WASI preview1 runtime.
- `wasm32-wasip2`, stable Rust 1.95.0: compiled and linked; runtime behavior was not tested.
- The tests cover relative target resolution, dangling links that later resolve to directories, preservation of an existing destination, and NUL rejection in either path.
- Scoped rustfmt and diff whitespace checks passed. Independent GPT 6.1 Sol xhigh code review of this base/candidate found no actionable findings; the reviewer inspected the source and did not rerun tests.

The full package test did not reach compilation in the offline environment because the pinned `rmcp` Git dependency was not cached. These results establish module behavior only. They do not establish a complete `codex-git-utils` or Codex WASI build. Other WASI portability work remains outside this change.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the focused module proof</summary>

Requires Rust 1.95.0, its WASI target standard libraries, and Node with `node:wasi`.

```sh
git clone --branch fix/git-utils-wasi-symlink https://github.com/JustYannicc/codex.git
cd codex
git checkout 84b7ecac53dec547820c2fd5bae94c1f02ce0861
codex_source="$PWD"
proof_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$proof_dir/src"
cat > "$proof_dir/Cargo.toml" <<'EOF'
[package]
name = "codex-wasi-platform-proof"
version = "0.0.0"
edition = "2024"
[dependencies]
libc = "=0.2.186"
thiserror = "=2.0.18"
walkdir = "=2.5.0"
[dev-dependencies]
tempfile = "=3.27.0"
EOF
cat > "$proof_dir/src/lib.rs" <<EOF
#[path = "$codex_source/codex-rs/git-utils/src/errors.rs"]
mod errors;
pub use errors::GitToolingError;
#[path = "$codex_source/codex-rs/git-utils/src/platform.rs"]
mod platform;
pub use platform::create_symlink;
EOF
rustup target add --toolchain 1.95.0 wasm32-wasip1 wasm32-wasip2
cargo +1.95.0 test --manifest-path "$proof_dir/Cargo.toml" -j 2
cargo +1.95.0 test --manifest-path "$proof_dir/Cargo.toml" --target wasm32-wasip1 --no-run -j 2
cargo +1.95.0 test --manifest-path "$proof_dir/Cargo.toml" --target wasm32-wasip2 --no-run -j 2
node --input-type=module - "$proof_dir" <<'JS'
import { WASI } from 'node:wasi';
import { readFile, readdir, mkdtemp, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
const deps = join(process.argv[2], 'target/wasm32-wasip1/debug/deps');
const binary = (await readdir(deps)).find(name => name.endsWith('.wasm'));
if (!binary) throw new Error('WASI test binary not found');
const sandbox = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'codex-wasi-symlink-'));
try {
  const wasm = join(deps, binary);
  const wasi = new WASI({
    version: 'preview1',
    args: [wasm, '--test-threads=1', '--nocapture'],
    env: {},
    preopens: { '/': sandbox },
  });
  const module = await WebAssembly.compile(await readFile(wasm));
  const instance = await WebAssembly.instantiate(module, wasi.getImportObject());
  process.exitCode = wasi.start(instance);
} finally {
  await rm(sandbox, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
JS
```

Both native and WASIp1 runs reported:

```text
test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

The tests use `tempfile::tempdir_in(".")` because this stable WASI target's `std::env::temp_dir()` panics. The WASI runtime exposes only a fresh temporary directory as its working directory.

</details>

items.title: Esc/Ctrl-C while a PermissionRequest hook runs leaves the turn stuck in "Working" (and a later hook `allow` still runs the command)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.162.1

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### Which model were you using?

any

### What platform is your computer?

Ubuntu

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

_No response_

### Codex doctor report

```json

```

### What issue are you seeing?

Pressing Esc or Ctrl-C while a `PermissionRequest` hook is still running interrupts the turn
(the `Interrupt` hook fires, "Conversation interrupted" is shown) but does not stop the hook or
cancel the pending approval. When the hook later returns:
- with no output, an approval dialog for the interrupted turn appears; after Esc on it, Codex
  shows "Working (… esc to interrupt)" indefinitely – no further hooks fire, a second Esc doesn't
  help (still busy after 60 s);
- with `{"decision":{"behavior":"deny"}}`, the same hang;
- with `{"decision":{"behavior":"allow"}}`, **the command runs although the user interrupted the
  turn** – silently: no dialog, nothing in the transcript (it still ends with "Conversation
  interrupted"), and the composer looks idle.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. In an empty scratch directory (not a git repo), start Codex with a PermissionRequest hook that
   takes a while and then exits 0 with no output:
   ```
   codex --no-daemon --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust -a on-request -s read-only \
     -c 'hooks.PermissionRequest=[{hooks=[{type="command",command="sleep 15",timeout=600}]}]'
   ```
2. Prompt: `Use your shell tool to run exactly this command: touch x.txt -- then reply with one word: done.`
3. While the status shows "Working … · Running hooks", press Esc (or Ctrl-C).
   → "Conversation interrupted"; the hook keeps running.
4. When the hook finishes (~15 s after it started), an approval dialog for `touch x.txt` appears
   below "Conversation interrupted". Press Esc.
   → "You canceled the request to run touch x.txt", "Failed (exit 1) touch x.txt", then
   "Working (… esc to interrupt)" forever (still there after 60 s), with the composer shown
   underneath.

Allow variant – same steps, with a hook script that waits and then allows:
```
cat > /tmp/allow-hook.sh <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
sleep 15
printf '%s\n' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PermissionRequest","decision":{"behavior":"allow"}}}'
SH
chmod +x /tmp/allow-hook.sh
codex --no-daemon --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust -a on-request -s read-only \
  -c 'hooks.PermissionRequest=[{hooks=[{type="command",command="/tmp/allow-hook.sh",timeout=600}]}]'
```
After step 3, no dialog appears, and ~15 s later `x.txt` exists.

### What is the expected behavior?

Interrupting the turn cancels the pending approval: the running PermissionRequest hook is
terminated (or its result ignored), no dialog appears afterwards, a late `allow` never runs the
tool, and the composer is usable again.

### Additional information

Reproduced with exactly the steps above (`sleep 15`: 1/1; the allow script: 1/1), and earlier with
a hook that waits for an external signal: 4/4 no-output (Esc ×3, Ctrl-C ×1), 1/1 deny, 1/1 allow. Keys other than Esc/Ctrl-C typed during the hook go to the composer and
don't affect the dialog. Two parallel tool calls each start their own PermissionRequest hook at once.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Windows package observed in the failing app's log stack: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64`. The current About-dialog version was not collected. An earlier October 15 troubleshooting session reported UI version 26.1007.71326; that earlier version should not be treated as the verified October 18 UI version.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Home, x64. Time zone: Asia/Hong_Kong (UTC+08:00).

### What issue are you seeing?

Installing and connecting the Cloudflare plugin from the Codex desktop plugin UI does not complete reliably. The plugin can initially appear installed while its associated app connection keeps spinning. Codex later displays “插件安装超时” (“Plugin installation timed out”) and removes the plugin through installation rollback.

On subsequent connection attempts, the desktop UI displays:

```text
OAuth authorization response issuer does not match the expected issuer
```

The desktop log confirms that the app-connection callback reaches the service, but `POST /aip/connectors/links/oauth/callback` returns HTTP 403 with exactly that error. This is a plugin/app connection flow, not merely a `codex mcp login` CLI failure.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence:
1. Open Settings → Plugins → Cloudflare in the Windows desktop app and install the plugin.
2. Start the associated Cloudflare app connection and follow the browser authorization flow.
3. Return to Codex. The associated app may remain loading, or the issuer-mismatch error appears.
4. In an earlier observed attempt, the installation waiting period expired after approximately ten minutes and the installed plugin was rolled back.

These observations include separate attempts; the earlier timeout and the later HTTP 403 records should not be interpreted as one uninterrupted trace.

### What is the expected behavior?

A valid Cloudflare authorization response should pass issuer validation and the associated app should become connected. If verification fails, show the specific actionable failure promptly rather than leaving the connection spinning until an installation timeout. Issuer validation should remain enforced.

### Additional information

#### Confirmed HTTP 403 evidence — October 18, 2026

| UTC | Asia/Hong_Kong (UTC+08:00) | HTTP status |
|---|---|---|
| 13:43:09.259 | 21:43:09.259 | 403 |
| 13:43:45.753 | 21:43:45.753 | 403 |
| 13:44:07.446 | 21:44:07.446 | 403 |

Sanitized, field-selected extracts from the same desktop main log (original line numbers 6387, 6746, and 6950). Unrelated fields and the original filename/path are deliberately omitted:

```text
2026-10-18T13:43:09.259Z warning [electron-message-handler] sa_server_request_failed method=post routePattern=/aip/connectors/links/oauth/callback status=403 errorMessage={"detail":{"message":"OAuth authorization response issuer does not match the expected issuer","connector_id":"[CLOUDFLARE_CONNECTOR_ID_REDACTED]"}}

2026-10-18T13:43:45.753Z warning [electron-message-handler] sa_server_request_failed method=post routePattern=/aip/connectors/links/oauth/callback status=403 errorMessage={"detail":{"message":"OAuth authorization response issuer does not match the expected issuer","connector_id":"[CLOUDFLARE_CONNECTOR_ID_REDACTED]"}}

2026-10-18T13:44:07.446Z warning [electron-message-handler] sa_server_request_failed method=post routePattern=/aip/connectors/links/oauth/callback status=403 errorMessage={"detail":{"message":"OAuth authorization response issuer does not match the expected issuer","connector_id":"[CLOUDFLARE_CONNECTOR_ID_REDACTED]"}}
```

#### Earlier timeout/rollback attempt — October 18, 2026, UTC+08:00

- 20:57:42: plugin installation began.
- 20:57:46: `plugin_install_succeeded` was logged.
- 20:58:05: a separately configured Cloudflare MCP server reported OAuth login completed. This is not proof that the plugin-associated app connection succeeded.
- The app exited at 20:58:15 and was relaunched; the pending installation state survived the restart.
- 21:07:42.585: persisted installation reconciliation deadline.
- 21:07:44.117: `plugin_uninstall_succeeded` for the same plugin.
- The corresponding persisted reconciliation state later showed `installed=true`, `oauthFailed=true`, `rolledBack=true`; its matching pending callback state was `claimed=false`, `completed=false`. These describe the retained reconciliation record, not a claim that the rolled-back plugin remained installed.

A later browser attempt also displayed:
```text
Temporarily Unavailable
Client metadata is temporarily unavailable. Please try again.
Error code: temporarily_unavailable
```
This was a separate observed failure. No HTTP status was captured for that browser page.

#### Scope and uncertainty

- The HTTP 403 proves that these later callback requests reached the service and were rejected at issuer validation.
- Neither the expected issuer nor the actual returned issuer is included in the retained log extracts. Please inspect the connector's issuer/discovery configuration and the actual authorization-response `iss` values for the timestamps above.
- It is not established whether this is an OpenAI connector configuration/cache issue or a Cloudflare issuer/metadata issue.
- A separate localhost callback page reported “Authentication complete”; that cannot establish success of the plugin-associated callback that returned 403.
- Related but different CLI report: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37300 (missing required issuer rather than this desktop app-connection HTTP 403).

#### Redaction

No OAuth authorization codes, tokens, cookies, state/PKCE values, full authorization/callback URLs, email addresses, user/account IDs, session/thread IDs, local usernames, or full local log files are included. Connector identifiers and local file paths have been redacted. Screenshots containing authorization URL fragments are not attached.

5. Observe continued investigation expansion and repeated need for human intervention instead of a clear completed deliverable plus a bounded statement of remaining work.

items.body:
Codex desktop imports claude-mem internal observer transcripts as user chats, flooding sidebar

Environment: macOS 27.0.1; ChatGPT desktop app 26.1002.52244 with Codex; installed claude-mem plugin 13.25.3. Observed 18 October 2026.

Observed behavior: the Codex sidebar contains dozens of imported chats titled "Condense the tool payload below to under 12800 characters". Local inspection found 96 JSONL transcripts under the Claude project-history directory corresponding to ~/.claude-mem/observer-sessions. The newest source transcript was modified 3 October 2026; we have not established ongoing generation. A representative imported chat contains a condensation prompt and an EXTERNAL SESSION IMPORTED marker. These are internal memory-processing sessions, not user-created project tasks.

Evidence: installed claude-mem worker source constructs this exact prompt when compressing oversized tool inputs/outputs and invokes a standalone Claude SDK observer session. Upstream independently documents the same chain: internal SDK transcripts enter normal ~/.claude/projects history and Codex imports them.
https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues/4689
https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/pull/4692

Upstream fix #4692 adds the opt-in CLAUDE_MEM_OBSERVER_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR transcript-location override. Installed 13.25.3 lacks that setting. This report concerns Codex import robustness as well as the plugin interaction; we are not asserting that OpenAI alone caused it.

Reproduction outline (not re-executed to avoid generating more private transcripts): use affected claude-mem with Claude SDK observer processing of large tool payloads; allow normal transcript persistence; import Claude conversations in Codex. Internal compression jobs appear as ordinary chats.

Expected: an import preview, exclusion mechanism, or reliable filtering of known internal observer sessions so routine memory processing does not pollute the user sidebar. Please advise the supported filtering/cleanup mechanism and whether imported payloads remain local or are synced/uploaded under the account's settings.

Privacy: no raw transcripts, screenshot, credentials, private source payloads, or personal project data are attached. We have not established unauthorized access or a security breach. Cost is unknown. Please treat this as an import/sidebar and privacy-boundary clarity report.

items.body:
macOS에서 ChatGPT/Codex를 이용하던 중, 작업 세션 생성 동의와 가시성, 모델·사용량 정보에 관한 심각한 문제를 경험해 조사와 개선을 요청합니다.

저는 개발 진행을 승인했지만, 별도 작업 세션을 생성하거나 그 세션에서 사용할 모델을 선택하는 것에 대해 사전에 구체적인 설명이나 확인을 받지 못했습니다. 이후 별도 작업으로 시작했다는 안내와 링크는 있었으나, 해당 세션을 사이드바나 대화 검색에서 찾을 수 없었습니다. 링크로는 열 수 있었습니다. 따라서 전혀 접근할 수 없었다는 주장은 아닙니다. 제가 직접 찾고 관리하기 어려운 세션에서 작업이 수행됐다는 점이 핵심입니다.

해당 화면에는 사용 한도에 도달했다는 메시지와 추가 크레딧 구매 또는 2026년 10월 22일 오전 7:24 이후 재시도 안내가 표시됐습니다. 안내에는 시간대나 어떤 한도가 적용됐는지 명확한 설명이 없었고, 모델 표시도 ‘Loading model…’ 상태였습니다.

반면 다른 대화에서는 응답이 가능했습니다. 지원팀의 자동 응답은 당시 주간 사용량이 약 5%라고 안내했습니다. 이것만으로 오류라고 단정할 수는 없지만, 해당 세션의 제한과 계정 사용량 사이의 관계를 사용자가 이해할 수 없었습니다. 실제 사용 모델·추론 설정·세션별 토큰 또는 크레딧 소비량도 확인하지 못했습니다.

다음 사항을 요청합니다.
1. 별도 세션 생성 경위와 당시 동의·안내 흐름을 조사해 주세요.
2. 생성된 모든 작업 세션을 사용자가 목록과 검색에서 찾아 관리할 수 있도록 해 주세요.
3. 세션별 실제 모델·추론 설정·사용량과 비용을 확인할 수 있게 해 주세요.
4. 해당 제한 메시지의 정확한 원인과 다른 대화가 가능한 이유를 설명해 주세요.
5. 이 사안에 대한 담당자의 검토와 개선 계획을 알려 주세요. 승인 범위를 벗어난 사용이나 잘못된 과금이 확인된다면 그에 대한 시정 조치도 요청합니다.

고의적인 은폐 여부를 단정하는 것은 아닙니다. 다만 사용자 입장에서는 세션과 자원 사용을 통제할 수 없었다는 심각한 신뢰 문제입니다. 원본 캡처와 상세 기록은 OpenAI 지원팀에 비공개로 제공했습니다. 계정 정보와 비공개 작업 내용은 공개 글에서 제외합니다.

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

A user-created private personal plugin is shown as installed in the Plugins UI, but it is unavailable in a new ChatGPT Work chat.

The same plugin has three mutually inconsistent installation states:

- The Plugins sidebar lists it under **Installed**, and its detail page labels it **Dein Cloud-Plugin** ("Your cloud plugin").
- A direct installation suggestion using the exact backend plugin ID returns `Already installed (already_installed)`.
- A permission lookup using that same exact backend plugin ID returns `status: not_installed`.
- An uninstall request using that same exact backend plugin ID reports that the plugin was not installed and removes nothing.

In a freshly loaded Work composer, searching the exact display name in the Plugins picker returns **Keine Plugins gefunden** ("No plugins found"), although other installed plugins are listed. The plugin's MCP tools are therefore not attached to the new Work chat and cannot be called.

This is not a local MCP availability report. The local runtime and transport were independently healthy, but no ChatGPT Work tool call occurred because the plugin could not be selected.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Sign in to a personal ChatGPT Pro account.
2. Create or open a user-owned plugin with:
   - scope `USER`
   - discoverability `PRIVATE`
   - one current release
   - one MCP server

items.title: [Windows desktop] Resuming chat spawns hundreds of binary git diff processes, escalating handles and PC crashes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop on Windows repeatedly destabilises the entire PC when an existing, long-lived chat is resumed. Captured evidence shows hundreds of background Git binary-diff processes and rapidly increasing Codex handles/descendants. In the best-documented incident, the resumed agent issued **no Git command** before the surge.

Possibly related to #53910: the captured per-file `git diff --binary --no-index` command pattern matches that report. This report concerns **Windows desktop**, not a verified Linux zombie leak, and does not establish the same underlying defect.

## Environment

- Windows 11; approximately 32 GB RAM.
- Codex Desktop, existing local Unity game repository with many image assets.
- Exact incident-time desktop/backend/Git versions were not captured in the available audit; no version attribution is intended.
- Very long-lived chat, with approximately 2.38 GB local rollout history. This is context, not a proven trigger.
- Times below: 18 October 2026, Europe/London (UTC+01:00).

## Observed trigger and agent activity

1. User resumed an existing chat after explicitly requiring one agent-issued Git command at a time, parent ownership of Git, no polling or repeated scans, and a stop on unexpected process growth.
2. The resumed turn acknowledged those rules. Recorded agent commands were targeted file reads and a CIM query of already-running Git processes.
3. No agent-issued Git command, new subagent launch, or Unity execution is recorded in that turn before interruption.
4. Root Git processes began around 06:20:48; recorded turn start was 06:20:50 and desktop `thread/read` was logged at 06:20:50.617.
5. Git counts, CPU and Codex handle counts rose rapidly; the PC subsequently rebooted. The user reports repeated crashes. A crash dump establishing the final failure mechanism is not available.

**Please do not request an uncontrolled reproduction on this machine:** simply resuming this chat appears sufficient to trigger severe resource growth.

## Captured measurements

| Local time | System CPU | Git processes | System processes | Main Codex handles | Main Codex descendants |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 06:20:56 | 58.30% | 86 | 363 | 7,285 | 187 |
| 06:21:08 | 96.64% | 192 | 529 | 17,719 | 345 |
| 06:21:20 | 96.00% | 303 | 697 | 27,270 | 515 |

A separate, later CIM snapshot counted **490 git.exe processes**; this is not simultaneous with the table rows.

Last durable sample: 06:21:20.607. Next Windows boot: 06:24:28.5. Existing diagnostic monitor resumed at 06:24:49.947.

An earlier incident around 04:56–04:58 saw Git processes grow 0 → 370, Codex handles 896 → 54,378, and Codex descendants 92 → 659 within approximately 85 seconds.

## Process evidence

Many root Git instances were directly parented by `codex.exe` PID 15388. Additional Git children carried the same command line. Representative command, with local project path redacted:

```text
"git" -c safe.bareRepository=explicit -c core.hooksPath=NUL -c core.fsmonitor=false diff --no-textconv --no-ext-diff --binary --no-index -- NUL "<project>/Assets/.../baseline.png"
```

Other captured paths were individual background, preview and character PNG assets.

The command explicitly disables hooks and fsmonitor. Parent/child Git pairs alone do not prove recursion; normal Git for Windows launcher behaviour must be distinguished from an actual loop.

## Expected behaviour

Background repository/review diff collection should have bounded concurrency, bounded output, cancellation, and deduplication/backpressure. Large sets of binary assets or reopening a chat should not cause machine-wide resource exhaustion. Agent instructions limiting Git cannot control desktop/backend work outside agent tool calls.

## Interpretation and uncertainty

Timing, parent PIDs, command lines, and absence of agent Git calls strongly implicate automatic Codex background diff activity. The precise internal feature, pipe/child lifetime bug, and final Windows resource allocator failure are **not proven**. Large history and asset volume are possible amplifiers, not established causes. The pipe-write mechanism reported in #53910 has not been measured on this Windows machine.

## Evidence retained locally

A targeted read-only audit, companion bounded process evidence, timestamped JSONL monitor samples, and desktop log excerpts are retained locally. Full raw logs, user paths, project content, and the enormous chat transcript are deliberately omitted from this public issue. A private support channel would be preferable for any additional sensitive evidence.

No Git configuration, security settings, or diagnostic monitor configuration was changed as a workaround. No processes were automatically killed during the audit.

items.title: Windows MXC sandbox leaves AppContainer named-object directories behind (`\Sessions\1\AppContainerNamedObjects\S-1-15-2-…`), growing until reboot

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems
