labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What happens

When Codex runs commands in the Windows MXC sandbox, some sandboxes are never fully released. Each command makes the Application Information service (Appinfo) create an AppContainer profile named `Sandbox.{GUID}`, along with an inbound and an outbound firewall block rule. When the command ends, the profile and the rules are deleted. For a fraction of the sandboxes, though, the kernel object directory `\Sessions\1\AppContainerNamedObjects\<AppContainer SID>` stays behind. The registry mapping for that SID is gone, and no live process has that AppContainer SID. The leftover directories accumulate until the machine restarts.

Related: #54400 reports token leaks in the restricted-token (elevated) sandbox. This issue is a separate signature in MXC mode; see the comparison below.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9711, ARM64
- Codex app (MSIX) `OpenAI.Codex` 26.1013.4894.0; codex-cli 0.163.0
- `~/.codex/.sandbox/sandbox.<date>.log` shows `Windows sandbox selection: mxc` from 2026-10-16 onward. That is the same day the leftover directories started piling up. MXC is selected even though `config.toml` has `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`.

### Evidence (17 h after a fresh restart, normal agent use)

Every 10 minutes a logger counted the following:
- entries in `\Sessions\1\AppContainerNamedObjects`, using `NtQueryDirectoryObject` (needs no elevation)
- live `Token` objects, using `NtQueryObject` with `ObjectTypesInformation`

| | At start | After 17 h |
|---|---|---|
| AppContainer named-object dirs | 9 | 109 |
| Token objects | 5,415 | 9,084 |

- Growth happens only in two bursts of Codex activity (05:30–06:50 and 12:00–13:10). The counts stay flat while Codex is idle.
- Over the same period, `Microsoft-Windows-AppModel-Runtime/Admin` logged 667 creates (event 39, "Successfully created AppContainer Sandbox.{GUID}") and 667 deletes (event 41). Every event was logged from the svchost process that hosts Appinfo. The profile create/delete calls are balanced.
- I passed each logged `Sandbox.{GUID}` name to `DeriveAppContainerSidFromAppContainerName`. 93 of the 94 leftover unmapped directories match a logged sandbox name. That is roughly 1 leaked directory per 7 sandboxes.
- None of those 94 SIDs belongs to a running process (checked via `GetTokenInformation(TokenAppContainerSid)` on every process). The references holding the directories open are therefore kernel-side; no user-mode handle holds them.
- Before the restart, after several days of heavier use, the same machine had 2,956 unmapped AppContainer directories and about 61.7k Token objects, but only about 2.4k open Token handles system-wide.

### What does not reproduce it

I measured directories, Token objects and the `Toke` paged-pool tag before and after each run below. For each run I used `codex sandbox -c 'windows.sandbox="<mode>"' -- cmd /c exit 0`, launched outside any app container.

| Mode | Runs | Sandboxes created | AppContainer dirs | Token objects | `Toke` paged pool |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mxc | 20 | 60 | +0 | −1 | −1 KB |
| elevated | 20 | 0 | +0 | +69 | +144 KB |

- In MXC mode, trivial commands clean up completely. The leak seen in real use depends on something these no-op runs don't do. Candidates are longer-running commands, commands that are cancelled or time out, child processes that outlive the command, and the app's own launch path (the app creates 2 sandboxes per command; the CLI creates 3). I haven't isolated the trigger yet.
- In elevated mode, these runs leak about 3.5 tokens per command. That is consistent with #54400, though smaller than the ~33 per command reported there.
- Booting WSL, other Windows processes, and other AI tools running shell commands did not create these sandboxes or directories in the same window.

### Expected

Once an MXC sandbox's command has exited and its profile has been deleted, nothing should still reference its AppContainer objects. Then the named-object directory and its tokens are freed.

### Impact

The leak is modest per day: about 100 directories and a few thousand tokens. The `Toke` paged-pool tag rose from about 14 MB to 18 MB. It is unbounded until restart, though. On this machine it reached about 3k directories and about 62k tokens before a restart.

### Workaround

Restart regularly. Per #54400, "Shut down" with Fast Startup enabled hibernates the kernel and does not clear the leak.

### Happy to provide

The per-10-minute samples (JSON lines), the event-log extracts and the measurement scripts.

### What issue are you seeing?

After selecting text, right-clicking, or Crtl+C, or any similar way, the codex TUI shows "Copy sent to terminal · paste to verify". However, it does not succeed in writing into my clipboard.

In contrast, using the same terminal but without SSH (using my local codex instead of the one on my server, same version 0.163.0 tui), it shows "Copied xxx chars to host clipboard", and it actually succeeded. This rules out the terminal issue mentioned in #52264 .

To rule out server issues too, I then tried 'ssh localhost'. The symptoms are still there - "Copy sent to terminal, paste to verify" and no actual clipboard write.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Open codex through a ssh connection.

### What is the expected behavior?

It should write my clipboard just like if it's on my computer.

If this is not possible, at least disable the crtl+c hook when ssh environment is detected. (I still want other features of the TUI so I'm not willing to switch to tui scrollback).

Native Computer Use can read CapCut's accessibility tree, capture its current window, and operate some native menus, but screenshot-based coordinate clicks and scrolling fail with:

```text
Computer Use server error -10005: noWindowsAvailable
```

A control test in macOS Calculator initially failed with the same error. Reacquiring Calculator by bundle ID and invoking its exposed window `Raise` action was followed by a successful coordinate click on 7, verified in both AX state and a fresh screenshot. The same recovery sequence did **not** restore coordinate input in CapCut.

This is an observed session reproduction, not a clean-install reproduction or proof of a shared internal root cause.

## Environment

Versions read from local installed metadata on 2026-10-18:

- macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434; arm64.
- ChatGPT/Codex desktop: 26.1013.40934, build 20770; bundle ID `com.openai.codex`.
- Codex Computer Use helper: 26.1013.1001501, build 1001501.
- CapCut: CFBundleShortVersionString `9.4.4639`; CFBundleVersion `9.5.7-beta1`.
- Native integration: `mcp__cua_repl.js` / `cua` API.

Earlier GUI checks showed Screen Recording and Accessibility enabled for Codex Computer Use and only the built-in display listed. Those checks were not repeated immediately before every attempt. Concurrent Computer Use activity in other chats was not independently audited.

## CapCut reproduction

1. With CapCut running, acquire it through `cua.getApp('com.lemon.lvoverseas')`. In the observed running state, acquisition succeeds and exposes the CapCut window with a `Raise` secondary action.
2. Invoke the latest window element's exposed `Raise` action.
3. Request a fresh AX state and screenshot. Both succeed.
4. Choose a visible harmless control from that screenshot and call `cap.click([x, y])`.
5. Observe immediate `-10005: noWindowsAvailable`. A subsequent AX read and screenshot still succeed, with no verified control activation.

On the home screen, clicking the project-search button at the observed screenshot coordinate `[1765, 1387]` failed. This is an example from that screenshot, **not** a portable coordinate. Coordinate scrolling and scrolling via an AX scroll-region index also failed with the same error.

Native AX menu actions still worked: the File menu could be opened and cancelled. Thus readable AX/screenshot state did not imply coordinate-input availability.

## Calculator control

Using the same Computer Use session:

1. `cua.getApp('/System/Applications/Calculator.app')` and `getScreenshot()` succeeded.
2. `calc.click([68, 422])`, the center of 7 in the observed 460×816 capture, failed with `noWindowsAvailable`; display unchanged.
3. Reacquire with `cua.getApp('com.apple.calculator')`.
4. Invoke the exposed window `Raise` action and capture fresh state.
5. Repeat `calc.click([68, 422])`.
6. This time no error; AX input value and screenshot both showed `7`.

There was no intermediate click between reacquisition and Raise, so this does not isolate which step helped or exclude an unrelated state change.

## Recovery attempts and subsequent acquisition errors

Reacquisition + Raise, menu cancellation, and a fresh screenshot did not fix CapCut coordinate clicks.

CapCut was then quit via its normal menu, and reacquisition/launch attempts produced additional errors:

- Outer full app path: `timeoutReached` on one attempt; later `Running application not found: com.lemon.lvoverseas`.
- Inner full app path: `timeoutReached`.
- Bundle ID:
  ```text
  Ambiguous app identifier 'com.lemon.lvoverseas'. Multiple apps share this bundle identifier: /Applications/CapCut.app, /Applications/CapCut.app/Contents/Frameworks/CapCut.app. Use an app name or full app path instead.
  ```

The duplicate identifiers were also confirmed in the two installed Info.plist files. These are nested bundles within one app; this is **not evidence of two separate installations**, and it does not establish that the ambiguity causes the coordinate failure. Full-path acquisition did not reliably recover the app.

A fallback Finder acquisition returned `cgWindowNotFound`.

Earlier attempts in this workflow included normal/fullscreen comparisons, CUA REPL reset, layout reset, and CapCut restart without a verified recovery. A fresh restart of the desktop app/helper was not performed in this latest comparison, so no claim is made about its effect here.

## Expected behavior / impact

Coordinate input should target the same app window successfully exposed by fresh capture and AX reads, or return an actionable diagnostic explaining the different target resolution.

This blocks GUI timeline editing and MP4 export. No completed edit or export is claimed from the failed actions.

## Related reports

- #43119 — same error and app-dependent coordinate failure; includes manual activation recovery and failures of Raise/restart in other apps.
- #46471 — readable Godot window/native menus, coordinate failure, then acquisition timeout.
- #36459 — fresh Safari state succeeds while coordinate input fails.

This adds a CapCut reproduction on newer installed desktop/helper builds, a successful Calculator control, and a nested-bundle acquisition ambiguity. Please merge/mark duplicate if these belong to the same issue.

No private project content, account details, raw logs, or screenshots are attached.

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

The official ChatGPT Library transfer helper fails during module loading on macOS with Python 3.9.6, before argument parsing, help output, authentication, or download. The failure was first observed during a Library materialization attempt on 2026-10-17 and reproduced with the unchanged helper's `--help` command on 2026-10-18.

This report asks for confirmation of the supported Python/runtime contract and the helper's owning component. **It does not assume that Python 3.9 is officially supported, or that the current distributed helper still matches the preserved copy.** If this integration is maintained outside `openai/codex`, please route the report to its owner.

Examined helper:

- Resource-relative path: `library/scripts/library_file_transfer.py`.
- Size: **11,084 bytes**.
- SHA-256: **`5e1557817be17db06e2375f8c34ed83e948d520242e5ee4cb50a30c7a4c83378`**.
- The historical workflow verified that this file matched the official resource fetched at that time. No helper-specific release version was declared in the examined file. The latest official resource could not be re-fetched in the subsequent diagnostic context.

Error, with the local directory redacted:

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<helper-dir>/library_file_transfer.py", line 97, in <module>
    library_file_id: str | None,
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'type' and 'NoneType'
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Environment: macOS/Darwin, arm64. The original default `python3` reported **3.9.6**; the follow-up startup reproduction used Apple Command Line Tools Python **3.9.6**. The desktop UI version and exact macOS release were not measured; no app version is inferred from a runtime bundle.

1. Obtain the official helper matching the size/hash above. Keep it unchanged.
2. In its directory, run with Python 3.9.6:

   ```sh
   python3 --version
   python3 -B library_file_transfer.py --help
   ```

3. Observe exit code **1**, empty stdout, and the TypeError above. No Library file, transfer manifest, signed URL, token, or network request is needed for this startup reproduction.
4. Invoke the same bytes with an already available newer interpreter and `-B library_file_transfer.py --help`.

Direct CLI startup results on 2026-10-18:

| Python | Result | Exit code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3.9.6 | TypeError at module line 97; no help | 1 |
| 3.12.14 | Help displayed | 0 |
| 3.14.7 | Help displayed | 0 |

The helper's hash was identical before and after these checks. Only startup/help was exercised; this table is **not** an end-to-end transfer or full Python compatibility certification.

### What is the expected behavior?

Please confirm:

1. **Official support matrix:** Which Python versions, operating systems, and local execution routes are supported for the Library helper? Should the workflow use a managed interpreter rather than the default `python3`?
2. **Current release:** What resource/helper version and SHA-256 are currently distributed, and is there an existing fix for this startup failure? Please identify the corrected version/commit if applicable.
3. **Implementation ownership:** Which team and actual source repository/file maintain this helper, and where should a focused contribution be proposed?

If Python 3.9 is supported, the helper should load under that supported version. If it is unsupported, the workflow should select a supported runtime or provide an explicit version requirement before incompatible module definitions execute, rather than an annotation TypeError. A check only inside `main()` cannot intercept this failure because line 97 is evaluated first.

### Additional information

- The examined file has another `str | None` annotation at line 169, no `from __future__ import annotations`, and no early `sys.version_info` check. Python 3.9 AST parsing succeeds. An in-memory compilation control using deferred annotations allows help startup; this isolates annotation evaluation but is not a proposed or applied patch.
- Related reports #49767 and #53414 concern Windows extended-attribute handling. This report fails earlier, during macOS/Python startup; those workarounds do not establish a fix for this failure.
- Exact helper/3.9 issue and PR searches did not identify a matching repair. This does not rule out differently named, unpublished, or staged fixes.
- No helper code was modified, no PR was created, and no interpreter or plugin was installed or updated for this diagnosis. No transfer or metadata-writing operation was run in the startup checks.
- This report omits private file/conversation identifiers, user/project paths, business content, transfer manifests, completion markers, signed URLs, credentials, cookies, and authentication headers. No raw session log or helper archive is attached.

items.body:
## Summary

The bundled Windows Computer Use plugin can enumerate DingTalk's main window, but `sky.get_window` rejects the fresh returned window with a contradictory ownership error. The expected and current app identifiers in the message are identical. Youdao desktop translation works through the same client: binding, screenshots, typing, clicking, and reading the translation all succeeded.

## Environment

- Windows desktop (exact OS build and desktop app version not collected)
- Computer Use plugin: `26.1013.40934`
- DingTalk executable product/file version: `9.0.2.261013001`
- Client: bundled `@oai/sky`, initialized in the Node REPL as instructed by the plugin skill
- Reproduced repeatedly on 2026-10-18

## Minimal reproduction

```js
const { sky } = await import('@oai/sky');
const windows = await sky.list_windows();
const candidates = windows.filter(w => w.title === '钉钉');
if (candidates.length !== 1) throw new Error('Expected one DingTalk window');
const returned = candidates[0];
const window = await sky.get_window({id: returned.id, app: returned.app});
```

Example fresh enumeration:

```json
{"app":"Microsoft.AutoGenerated.{17F98C31-0FDC-A7D8-8C79-66D85764ED87}","id":263964,"title":"钉钉"}
```

Actual error:

```text
window id 263964 no longer belongs to Microsoft.AutoGenerated.{17F98C31-0FDC-A7D8-8C79-66D85764ED87}; current owner is Microsoft.AutoGenerated.{17F98C31-0FDC-A7D8-8C79-66D85764ED87}
```

## Observations and troubleshooting

- Refreshing `list_windows` and immediately binding its returned object still fails.
- Reopening DingTalk produced different window IDs but the same error.
- Omitting `app` from `get_window({id})` also failed in an earlier attempt.
- Capturing a freshly enumerated Window directly through `get_window_state` also failed.
- `launch_app` reports no targetable window, but a subsequent `list_windows` finds DingTalk's main window.
- An earlier `list_apps` result had both a process-path DingTalk entry with no windows and a Chinese-named auto-generated-ID entry owning the main window. This is an observation, not a confirmed root cause.
- Youdao desktop app works in the same setup, so the failure is not universal across applications.
- No DingTalk screenshot was obtained; screenshot protection or an accessibility-tree issue has not been established.
- Elevation differences have not been established.

## Expected behavior

A freshly returned DingTalk window should bind when expected and current owners match, or the error should expose the actual reason for rejection.

## Related reports

- #36335 (Blender; similar app-specific failure and contradictory owner message)
- #37484 (identical process-owner error)
- #50032 (Access; another desktop application works in the same setup)

No account details, organization details, course links, authentication data, or session logs are attached.

2. Execute a basic command through the default sandbox. Commands such as whoami and node --version succeed.
3. Submit an exec_command request with sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated".

   "The automatic permission approval review did not finish before its deadline."

Automatic approval review should complete with an approval decision. Approved commands should execute normally, while denied requests should provide a clear reason.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1013.40934

### What subscription do you have?

Unknown (not provided)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-38-generic x86_64 x86_64

### What issue are you seeing?

When ChatGPT Desktop is open but Codex has no active local task and is waiting for the user, Cinnamon Session Manager still reports a suspend inhibitor attributed to the app. This can prevent normal suspend and may interfere with hibernation.

Observed on this machine:
- App ID: `/usr/lib/chatgpt/ChatGPT`
- Inhibitor reason: `Electron`
- Cinnamon Session Manager inhibitor flags: `4` (inhibits suspending the session/computer)
- `login1.Manager.CanSuspend` returned `yes`; `login1.Manager.CanHibernate` returned `no`.

The separate `systemd-inhibit` entry for ChatGPT lists `shutdown`; that entry alone does not demonstrate a sleep inhibitor. The Cinnamon D-Bus inhibitor above is the specific sleep-related observation. The cause of `CanHibernate = no` is not established, and actual hibernate/resume has not yet been tested.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Linux Mint Cinnamon (X11), launch ChatGPT Desktop.
2. Leave Codex idle, or let a turn finish so the app is waiting for the user's next message/approval.
3. Inspect the Cinnamon Session Manager inhibitor list using its D-Bus `GetInhibitors` method.
4. Query the returned inhibitor object's `GetAppId`, `GetReason`, and `GetFlags` methods.
5. In this report, the idle app was still present with app ID `/usr/lib/chatgpt/ChatGPT`, reason `Electron`, and flags `4`.
6. For comparison, run `systemd-inhibit --list --no-pager` and query login1's `CanSuspend` and `CanHibernate` methods.

### What is the expected behavior?

While Codex is actively executing a local task, ChatGPT Desktop should hold the appropriate session inhibitor so the computer does not suspend or hibernate and interrupt the work. As soon as the turn ends or pauses for human input (approval, clarification, or a response), the app should release the inhibitor and keep it released while idle, allowing normal desktop power management. Actual hibernation remains subject to OS/hardware support and configuration.

### Additional information

Feedback session ID: 01a14a88-f0aa-7d70-b949-8f5f940e3db3

ChatGPT Desktop package version: 26.1013.40934 (reported by the installed Linux package).
System: Linux Mint 22.3 Zena, Cinnamon 6.6.9, X11; kernel 7.0.0-38-generic; systemd 255.4-1ubuntu8.18.
Hardware: Lenovo IdeaPad S340-15IWL, Intel Core i5-8265U, 20 GiB RAM.

labels.name: TUI

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### Environment

Windows 11, native Windows Codex CLI, MSYS2 UCRT64, Bash, and mintty.

### Steps to reproduce

The original reproduction was on codex-cli 0.148.0:

1. Launch the native Windows Codex CLI from Bash in MSYS2 UCRT64 using mintty.
2. Type text into the prompt editor with the default newline bindings.
3. Press Shift+Enter and, separately, Ctrl+J.

Neither shortcut inserts a newline. Plain Enter submits the prompt.

### Expected behavior

Shift+Enter and Ctrl+J should insert a newline without requiring global mintty key remapping. Plain Enter should submit the prompt.

### Input diagnostics and local workaround

The diagnostics led to a local workaround: only on Windows when `MSYSTEM` is present and `TERM_PROGRAM=mintty`, normalize `KeyCode::Enter` with exactly `KeyModifiers::CONTROL` to `KeyCode::Enter` with `KeyModifiers::SHIFT` before forwarding the event to the TUI.

Codex uses Win32 input records on this path. In contrast, reading raw input in Bash shows that Ctrl+J produces LF (`0a`), so inspecting stdin bytes alone does not describe the key event received by the native Windows TUI.

### Current status and verification

We continue to maintain this workaround for 0.163.0. The release build and both normalization regression tests pass. Those tests check conversion in the affected environment and preservation of events outside it, including preservation of Ctrl+Shift+Enter.

A fresh interactive reproduction on an unpatched 0.163.0 has not yet been performed. The tests verify the normalization function, not the complete physical keyboard/input pipeline.

This is a local workaround rather than a proposed universal fix: it may also affect an intentional Ctrl+Enter binding in this environment if the input layer cannot distinguish the combinations.

### Related discussion

https://github.com/openai/codex/discussions/14104 includes a report of both Shift+Enter and Ctrl+J failing in MSYS2 UCRT64.

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex repeatedly terminates an existing EV charger development Goal
with codexErrorInfo: cyberPolicy.

The work concerns a user-owned EV charger PWA and firmware.
The last development response before the failures described UART
receive-timeout validation. We suspect a false positive, but the
specific triggering content has not been identified.

The native Goal resume request is accepted. A subsequent turn then
fails, and the Goal returns to blocked.

The recorded provider error is:
"This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk. If this
seems wrong, try rephrasing your request. If you’re doing authorized
security work that requires more cyber permissive safeguards, apply
for Daybreak access via
https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/status-and-access
before retrying."

Affected thread:
01a13e36-ee62-7c00-a991-c64e19b2dd7a

Recorded failures on 2026-10-18, Asia/Seoul (UTC+09:00):
17:13:17 — 01a14e07-2430-72b3-8ad7-ed2a73a074d1
17:25:18 — 01a14e1c-fc33-7810-aeae-a388e09c4171
17:31:35 — 01a14e22-f5c1-78b0-81cb-fad52a7a3015

Please investigate whether these failures are false positives.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Uploaded thread: 01a13962-55f3-7842-88fb-e97f8699b8af

### What is the expected behavior?

Legitimate EV charger software development should continue when
it complies with applicable policies.

If an operation is blocked, the available diagnostics should help
identify the affected operation and the appropriate review or
recovery procedure.

### Additional information

Affected execution:
- Codex CLI 0.160.0
- macOS, Apple Silicon
- gpt-6.1-sol, high reasoning effort
- Native Goals through app-server over stdio
- Discord provides the user interface

The current interactive CLI is 0.162.1. Reproduction on the latest
release, 0.163.0, has not been tested.

The doctor report was generated using the affected 0.160.0 binary
from the bridge directory in a non-interactive diagnostic invocation.
It does not reproduce every worker or per-thread configuration.

Environment
- Windows NT 10.0, build 26300.9711, DisplayVersion 26H2 (read from the host registry after the incident; not captured inside the failed child). Registry ProductName reports Windows 10 Pro; that label is reported verbatim rather than inferred from the build.
- @openai/codex 0.162.0; platform package 0.162.0-win32-x64; Node 24.18.0.
- Native Codex SHA256: dce685d569526ef4712fa82d20ff20e1309baad5fcd34215e1126698f611242f.
- Node SHA256: 9a4eb5f1c29c6a2e93852ead46b999e284a6a5ca8bab4d4e241d587d025a52de.
- codex.js SHA256: 61b0194f3bb6534439c8d26a3ed57d0805f84b884588b761795323eeb92fcf70.
- Git executable: C:/Program Files/Git/mingw64/bin/git.exe. Git version was not captured in the retained receipt.

Observed setup and failure
Codex app-server was launched via pinned Node/codex.js with windows.sandbox="mxc", default_permissions="auro-pilot-mxc", approval_policy="never", network disabled, and app-server --listen stdio://. A Node command was submitted through command/exec with the checkout as its requested cwd. It spawned Git with piped output and no separate cwd override.

The effective non-null filesystem configuration was compared exactly with the requested 28-entry table before command execution; comparison passed. The raw config/read response and resolved native policy were not retained. The table contains :root=deny, :minimal=read, temporary-root denies, an explicit checkout-directory read grant, selected worktree/common Git metadata and object-store read grants, pinned Git executable/DLL read grants, and protected-directory denies. No explicit checkout-ancestor grants were present. There were no write grants. This is a policy summary, not the complete configuration.

Ancestor traversal, policy translation, child enforcement and host filesystem rules remain hypotheses, not findings. We are not proposing broader parent/root permissions.

Reproduction limits and request

It omits the full original launch/configuration, repository layout, native policy expansion and host security state. The anonymized command was not executed; no minimal reproduction has been tested. items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?
26.1013.31256, build 20586, production channel (reported by the app updater on 18 October 2026).

### Platform
Windows NT 10.0.26300.0; local desktop execution with Windows filesystem paths, not WSL.

### Observed issue
Chrome browser tasks previously worked in an existing conversation. Following a desktop update, browser tasks can no longer start from that conversation.

Confirmed observations:
- Local configuration enables the Chrome, Browser and Unified Computer Use plugins.
- App logs on 18 October report `server=cua_repl status=ready` for the affected conversation, with no startup error on those lines.
- The agent's current callable tool inventory does not include a CUA/browser-control entry point.
- An older `chrome_extension__getTabContext` entry is listed, but calling it returns `Unsupported dynamic tool namespace: chrome_extension`.
- Repeated requests including an explicit `@Chrome` message did not expose a usable browser-control tool.
- An earlier user-provided screenshot showed the extension sidebar displaying “ChatGPT for Chrome is coming soon”.

### Important uncertainty
The updater currently reports `restart_required`. This may be an incomplete update/reconnection or a conversation tool-loading problem; the root cause is not established. Successful CUA service startup does NOT verify that the Chrome extension itself is connected. Extension version, current browser discovery and website permissions could not be checked because the browser tool is unavailable. We have not independently verified reproduction in a fresh chat.

### Expected behavior
A browser-enabled local conversation should expose the supported control tool and discover the authorized browser. If a restart, connection step, rollout restriction or unsupported state prevents this, the app should surface an actionable status instead of advertising an unusable context tool.

### Related report
#55018 describes Chrome being absent from browser discovery. The symptom here occurs earlier: the conversation cannot call the browser-control tool at all. These may be related; please consolidate if appropriate.

No credentials, account identifiers, local usernames, conversation transcripts, raw logs or business data are attached. No security protections or vendor MCP manifests were modified.


### Follow-up after user-reported restart — 18 October 2026
The user reports fully restarting both the desktop app and Chrome. A subsequent check in this same conversation still exposes no callable CUA/browser-control entry point, and the older Chrome context call still returns `Unsupported dynamic tool namespace: chrome_extension`. The app updater still reports version `26.1013.31256`, build `20586`, production channel, with status `restart_required` after the reported restart. The restart itself was reported by the user, not independently observed. This does not establish the cause of the persistent restart status. Browser control remains unavailable; no fresh-chat reproduction has been independently verified.


### Verified post-update and independent-session comparison — 18 October 2026
A further restart completed the pending update: the app now reports `26.1013.40934`, build `20770`, production, `up_to_date`. In the affected original conversation, browser-control tools remain absent and the legacy Chrome context namespace remains unsupported. An independent review agent in the same task DOES expose the supported CUA tool and successfully enumerated browsers. Its inventory contains a Chrome connection, but its extension instance identity differs from the original conversation's fixed authorized browser binding. The review stopped without selecting another instance or accessing any site, consistent with that binding restriction. This comparison suggests conversation capability/binding refresh needs investigation; it does not establish an implementation root cause. Related reports #54972 and #54545 describe existing-chat tool loss and recovery in a fresh chat. Instance IDs and private browser details are intentionally omitted.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Version 26.1013.40934  Released 16 Oct 2026

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro 100

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 (64-bit, x64) — running Codex Desktop version 26.1013.40934, connected to a remote Linux server via SSH.

### What issue are you seeing?

**Title: [Windows Codex Desktop] Remote SSH projects disappear after power interruption; re-adding does not restore Projects sidebar**

**Environment**
- Codex Desktop: 26.1013.40934 (released 16 October 2026)
- Windows 11
- Incident: 18 October 2026
- Remote Linux host: `bim-teksys`
- SSH connections: TeksysALGO, TeksysDPR, TeksysERP and TeksysBIM

**Issue**

Following an unexpected Windows power interruption, all four remote SSH projects disappeared from the Codex Desktop Projects sidebar.

All four SSH connections remain enabled and show Connected under Settings → Connections → SSH.

Existing remote conversations can be opened through Recents, but Projects continues to display "No projects".

**Steps attempted**
1. Reconnected the existing remote SSH host.
2. Re-added the four remote projects using Add Remote Project.
3. Verified that the remote project directories exist.
4. Confirmed that the remote SQLite database passes integrity checks.
5. Confirmed that 482 remote conversation records and session files remain present.
6. Checked project-registration persistence: the inspected remote database still reports zero projects and zero project roots.

**Expected behaviour**

Existing remote SSH projects should reappear in Projects, with their historical conversations accessible under the appropriate project.

**Actual behaviour**

The Projects sidebar remains empty despite successful SSH connections and project re-add attempts.

**Data preservation**

A verified backup of the remote database and 482 session files has been created. No manual database repair has been attempted.

**Request**

Please investigate remote SSH project registration, migration and sidebar persistence in Codex Desktop 26.1013.40934 and provide a supported recovery procedure.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install and open Codex Desktop for Windows, version 26.1013.40934 (released 16 October 2026).
2. Configure remote SSH connections to a Linux server through Settings → Connections → SSH.
3. Add four existing remote development projects: TeksysALGO, TeksysDPR, TeksysERP and TeksysBIM.
4. Open and use multiple Codex conversations associated with these remote working directories.
5. On 18 October 2026, an unexpected power interruption caused the Windows computer to shut down.
6. After restoring power and restarting Windows, launch Codex Desktop.
7. Observe that the Projects sidebar displays **"No projects"**, although all four SSH connections remain enabled and show **Connected**.
8. Open the previous remote conversations through Recents. They remain accessible.
9. Attempt to restore the projects using Add Remote Project / Ctrl+O and select the original remote directories.
10. Observe that the Projects sidebar remains empty after re-adding the projects.

### Additional diagnostic findings

- Remote Linux server: `bim-teksys`
- Remote Codex database integrity: `ok`
- Remote conversation records: 482
- Remote project records: 0
- Remote project-root records: 0
- Remote conversation assignments: 0
- Windows Codex migration flags: `projectsMigrated=True`, `threadAssignmentsMigrated=False`
- All four remote SSH connections display Connected.
- No Restart or Update notice is displayed.
- A verified backup of the remote database and 482 session files exists.

### Reproducibility

The original disappearance occurred after an unexpected power interruption. Re-adding remote projects has repeatedly failed to repopulate the sidebar. The power interruption itself has not been deliberately reproduced.

### Expected result

Existing remote SSH projects and their historical conversations should remain accessible and correctly grouped under Projects after restarting Codex Desktop.

### Actual result

Remote conversations remain accessible under Recents, but Projects continues to display "No projects".

### Request

Please investigate Codex Desktop's remote SSH project persistence, migration and sidebar loading, and provide a supported recovery procedure that preserves existing conversation history.

### What is the expected behavior?

After restarting Codex Desktop, all previously configured remote SSH projects should automatically reappear in the **Projects sidebar**, preserving their original names, remote working directories, and historical conversation associations.

Specifically:

1. TeksysALGO, TeksysDPR, TeksysERP and TeksysBIM should remain visible under Projects.
2. Each project should display its previously associated Codex conversations.
3. Existing SSH connections should remain functional after a Windows restart or unexpected shutdown.
4. If a project disappears, re-adding its original remote directory should restore its sidebar entry without losing or duplicating historical conversations.
5. Project registrations and conversation associations should persist reliably across application restarts and updates.

**Expected outcome:** Users should be able to resume their existing remote development projects and conversations without manually reconstructing their project organisation or modifying SQLite databases.

### Additional information

### Environment and diagnostic evidence

**Application**
- Codex Desktop for Windows, version 26.1013.40934
- Released: 16 October 2026
- Incident date: 18 October 2026
- Remote Linux server: `bim-teksys`
- SSH host alias: `teksys-server`

**Affected remote projects**
- TeksysALGO: `/opt/teksys-algo`
- TeksysDPR: `/opt/dpr-teksys`
- TeksysERP: `/opt/erp-teksys`
- TeksysBIM: `/opt/bim-teksys/teksysbim`

All four remote directories exist. Under Settings → Connections → SSH, all four connections are enabled and show **Connected**, with no Restart or Update notice.

### Database investigation

The remote Codex SQLite database at `/home/teksys/.codex/state_5.sqlite` was inspected in read-only mode.

Results:
- Database integrity: `ok`
- Historical conversation records: 482
- Registered projects: 0
- Project-root records: 0
- Conversations assigned to projects: 0
- Session files on disk: 482

Windows Codex configuration reported:
- `projectsMigrated = True`
- `threadAssignmentsMigrated = False`
- `local-projects` was empty during the final inspection.

### Troubleshooting performed

1. Verified the original remote source directories.
2. Reconnected the existing SSH host.
3. Attempted to re-add all four remote projects.
4. Confirmed historical conversations remain accessible through Recents.
5. Verified database integrity and saved session files.
6. Examined remote app-server processes and diagnostic logs.
7. Confirmed the Codex control socket has a legitimate active listener.
8. Inspected Windows Codex Desktop logs for project-registration and migration errors.

No definitive project-registration error was identified in the inspected logs.

### Data preservation

A consistent SQLite backup and copies of all 482 remote session files were created and validated successfully.

No manual SQLite modifications, migration-flag changes, project-ID reassignment, or application-data resets have been performed.

### Additional observations

The Windows power interruption affected the desktop computer, not the remote Linux server. Remote Codex conversations remain accessible, indicating that the primary unresolved issue concerns project registration, persistence, or sidebar visibility.

Re-adding remote projects does not restore the Projects sidebar. The inspected remote SQLite database continues to show zero project registrations after these attempts.

The database results do not establish whether the desktop application uses an additional project store.

**Engineering assistance requested:** Please identify the cause of the lost remote project registrations and provide a supported recovery method that preserves the original remote conversations and their project associations.

items.title: [Windows][Plus][CLI] GPT-6.1 Sol missing from both catalogs and HTTP 400 via built-in OpenAI provider; official-auth custom path behaves differently

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

items.body:
## Bug report: paid-account model availability is inconsistent across Codex provider paths

**This is a reproducible model-access and client/catalog consistency issue affecting a ChatGPT Plus subscriber.** I am reporting a technical failure, not claiming that any specific model substitution or intentional "silent downgrade" has been proven.

The same account can see GPT-6.1 Sol in the ChatGPT/Work web experience, yet the Windows Codex CLI's **resolved and bundled model catalogs omit `gpt-6.1-sol`**, and explicitly selecting it through the built-in `openai` provider returns HTTP 400. Meanwhile, a `custom` provider configuration using **ChatGPT/OpenAI authentication**, **without an alternate `base_url`**, was able to produce a response when passed that model slug. This inconsistent behavior should not be left unexplained for paying users.

### Environment (sanitized)

- Subscription: **ChatGPT Plus**; authentication reported as **`Logged in using ChatGPT`**.
- Platform: Windows 11, x64; PowerShell.
- Codex CLI: **`codex-cli 0.153.4`**.
- Client request settings tested: `--model gpt-6.1-sol`, `model_reasoning_effort="xhigh"`, read-only sandbox.
- CC Switch is installed for provider management. Its selected entry was shown as **OpenAI Official / direct**; the user-level Codex configuration contained the following **non-secret** provider configuration:

```toml
model_provider = "custom"

[model_providers.custom]
name = "OpenAI"
requires_openai_auth = true
supports_websockets = true
wire_api = "responses"
# No base_url specified in this provider block
```

No bearer tokens, account IDs, email addresses, private filesystem paths, session IDs, or raw TRACE logs are included in this public report.

### Reproduction A: built-in OpenAI provider returns HTTP 400

With an active ChatGPT login:

```powershell
codex login status
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only -c 'model_provider="openai"' -m gpt-6.1-sol -c 'model_reasoning_effort="xhigh"' "Reply with OK only."
```

The CLI startup banner confirmed:

```text
model: gpt-6.1-sol
provider: openai
reasoning effort: xhigh
warning: Model metadata for `gpt-6.1-sol` not found. Defaulting to fallback metadata; this can degrade performance and cause issues.
```

The request failed, twice reporting the same backend error:

```json
{"type":"error","status":400,"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"The 'gpt-6.1-sol' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}}
```

This is not an answer-quality issue or a prompt misunderstanding. **The selected model request is rejected outright.**

### Reproduction B: catalog disagreement

Using the same signed-in Codex CLI, I ran:

```powershell
codex debug models
codex debug models --bundled
```

The resolved catalog reported 6 entries:

```text
gpt-6-astra
gpt-reserve              [hidden]
gpt-5.6-sol
gpt-5.6-terra
gpt-5.6-luna
codex-auto-review        [hidden]
```

The bundled catalog reported 11 entries, adding older/other model entries but **still no `gpt-6.1-sol` or `gpt-6-sol`**. This directly accounts for the fallback-metadata warning, but does not explain why the web experience and Codex provider paths disagree.

### Reproduction C: official-auth custom path behaves differently

Before forcing `model_provider="openai"`, I launched a fresh, read-only `codex exec` session using `gpt-6.1-sol` and `xhigh`. The startup banner reported `provider: custom` and the same unknown-model/fallback warning, yet the session produced a full answer to a reasoning problem. This custom provider was configured as `requires_openai_auth = true` and had no third-party `base_url` set.

**Important limitation:** A successful answer under that model slug is **not proof of which underlying model weights actually served it**. The point is that the two provider configurations yield materially different outcomes under apparently official account authentication. Please investigate the request construction, model allowlist/catalog resolution and backend entitlement checks for each path.

### Expected behavior

1. If this paid account is entitled to GPT-6.1 Sol on Codex CLI, the model should be exposed consistently in the resolved model catalog and should execute successfully using the built-in `openai` provider.
2. If rollout, plan, workspace, region, or client-version restrictions apply, the CLI should surface the actual restriction **before execution** and provide actionable, precise guidance. An apparently valid model selection followed by an opaque HTTP 400 is not acceptable UX.
3. Model catalog metadata, the model picker, actual request acceptance, and server-reported model identity should not silently disagree. A custom provider reusing official authentication should not mysteriously bypass or change the visible availability contract without explanation.

### Actual user impact and paid-plan concern

I subscribed to **Plus** with the reasonable expectation that announced and account-visible Codex model features would be usable consistently across supported interfaces. Instead, I spent substantial time on reproducibility checks, only to find that a named model is missing from the CLI catalog and rejected by the backend.

**This is a frustrating and unacceptable experience for a paid product.** Customers should not have to reverse-engineer two catalog sources, switch provider IDs, inspect fallback-metadata warnings, or generate low-level logs to discover that a model visible on one product surface is inaccessible on another.

I am **not alleging fraud or proving intentional shadow routing**. But an unexplained disparity that feels like a downgrade to the end user deserves more than a generic answer such as "not supported." If this is expected rollout gating, document it transparently and explain why the same account sees different availability; if this is a regression, acknowledge and fix it.

### Actionable requests to maintainers

- Please verify GPT-6.1 Sol entitlement/catalog publication for **ChatGPT Plus + Windows Codex CLI** and clarify what the `gpt-6.1-sol` 400 means for an account where the model is visible on the web.
- Compare the request metadata and provider-routing behavior of built-in `openai` versus a `custom` provider with `requires_openai_auth=true` and no `base_url`.
- Explain and fix why **both** `codex debug models` catalogs omit GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Sol in this environment, especially when the product UI may expose them elsewhere.
- Make fallback model metadata, unsupported model IDs and provider/entitlement mismatches clearly actionable, with a non-secret diagnostic command.
- Provide an official statement on whether this is an unsupported client version, incomplete rollout, account entitlement sync bug, stale managed app-server, or backend incident. Please don't close with a generic "works as designed" unless the design is documented.
- For paying subscribers affected by a verified access regression, please indicate the support route for service restoration and consideration of a proportionate subscription remedy.

### Related reports / documentation

- #51308 — Windows Plus users missing GPT-6 Sol / GPT-6.1 Sol / GPT-6 Luna in the model picker.
- #49703 — GPT-6.1 Sol missing from CLI and explicit ChatGPT-login request rejected with an identical HTTP 400, on macOS.
- #50287 — stale managed app-server version can explain some CLI catalog/availability mismatches.
- #54293 — recent Windows Plus report: GPT-6.1 Sol missing from Codex desktop model picker.
- Official Help Center: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001275-chatgpt-work-and-codex (states GPT-6.1 Sol is rolling out for eligible paid plans, subject to plan/workspace/rollout).

**Distinct evidence here:** side-by-side built-in OpenAI provider rejection versus a ChatGPT-authenticated custom provider response, alongside exact resolved/bundled catalog contents and a fully redacted reproducible CLI command.

I can privately provide diagnostic records to OpenAI Support using an approved secure channel if the maintainers identify which redacted fields are needed. I will not post raw authentication logs publicly.

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: app

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex App (Windows), Codex Web, ChatGPT Desktop and ChatGPT Web

### What feature would you like to see?

## How a Unified Project Experience Could Work

### One Project. Multiple Work Modes. One Clear Identity.

Imagine opening ChatGPT or Codex and selecting a single project called **Project name**.

Regardless of whether I use ChatGPT Desktop, ChatGPT Web, Codex Desktop, or Codex Cloud, I should immediately know that I am working within the same project.

### Project: Project name

- **ChatGPT – Discussions and Planning:** Ideas, requirements, architecture, troubleshooting, and decisions.
- **Codex Local – Development:** Working directly with local source files and development sessions.
- **Codex Cloud – Cloud Development:** Development tasks through cloud environments.
- **GitHub – Source Control:** Repositories, branches, commits, and version history.

These are different work modes within one logical project, not four separate projects with the same name.

### Important: Not Everything Needs to Be Synchronized

I am not asking for every local file, conversation, development session, or technical operation to be uploaded to the cloud or displayed everywhere.

I appreciate local development and want to keep it.

Each environment can retain its own data, functionality, and technical limitations. What matters is a **common project identity**, with clear labels showing whether I am working locally, in the cloud, or with a connected repository.

### Example: Unified Project Dashboard

| Work Mode | Purpose | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ChatGPT | Discussions and planning | Cloud |
| Codex Local | Source code development | Local computer |
| Codex Cloud | Development tasks | Cloud |
| GitHub | Repository and version control | Connected service |

Users should be able to select a work mode within a project, just as they can select an AI model.

The interface should always make clear:
- Which project is currently active.
- Which work mode is being used.
- What is stored locally or in the cloud.
- Which GitHub repositories and local folders are linked.
- What is synchronized and what is not.

### Benefits for OpenAI: Modular Products and Flexible Pricing

A shared project identity would also let OpenAI evolve its products and pricing independently.

OpenAI could introduce new models, offer distinct subscription tiers, charge separately for advanced Codex or cloud capabilities, and add new work modes without requiring users to reorganize their projects.

There would be no need to put all the eggs in one basket or tightly couple every feature into one product.

A stable project foundation could support multiple independently evolving tools, business models, and execution environments.

### Why I Care

I genuinely love ChatGPT, Codex, and the ability to switch between projects, discuss ideas, develop software, and work directly with local files.

I see this as the future of software development, especially for individual developers and small teams where one person performs many different roles.

This is not a complaint. It is constructive feedback from an enthusiastic user who wants an already fantastic product to become even better.

**One project. Different tools. Independent environments. Flexible pricing. One coherent experience.**

### Additional information

Why I am passionate about this feature

First, I want to emphasize how much I genuinely love ChatGPT, Codex, and the new desktop experience.

The ability to move naturally between discussing ideas, planning features, solving technical problems, and developing real applications with AI is absolutely fantastic.

items.title: send_message_to_thread fails with "'sendRequest.bind' is not a function." from an ephemeral side chat, while the identical call succeeds from a regular chat

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Summary

Sending a message to an existing target thread succeeds from a regular chat but fails from an ephemeral side chat.

In a controlled comparison, both calls used the same tool, target thread ID, hostId, and prompt. The regular-chat call succeeded and received an acknowledgement from the target thread. The side-chat call returned isError: true with the following error:

'sendRequest.bind' is not a function.

## Environment

- Platform: macOS; the exact OS version was not collected
- Product: Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app
- App display name: ChatGPT
- Bundle ID: com.openai.codex
- App version: 26.1007.71326
- Build: 20398
- Incident date: October 18, 2026
- Time zone: Asia/Seoul, UTC+09:00
- Tool: tools.mcp__codex_app__send_message_to_thread
- Tool namespace: mcp__codex_app
- Outer execution tool: functions.exec

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Leave an existing target thread idle.
2. From a regular chat, invoke send_message_to_thread using the arguments below.
3. Confirm that the target thread receives the message and returns the requested acknowledgement.
4. From an ephemeral side chat, invoke the same tool once with exactly the same arguments.
5. Inspect the complete return object and the target thread's latest received turns.

The user explicitly authorized both test transmissions. The optional model and thinking arguments were omitted in both calls.

```javascript
const result = await tools.mcp__codex_app__send_message_to_thread({
  threadId: "01a13dfe-e475-7a52-a26d-d510bbb07869",
  hostId: "local",
  prompt: "[MCP 비교 점검 MCP_COMPARE_20261018_01] 기존 업무를 재개하지 마세요. 파일·코드·DB·Git 변경과 다른 채팅 전송 없이, 이 메시지에 'MCP_COMPARE_20261018_01 수신' 한 줄만 답하고 종료하세요."
});
text(result);
```

The Korean prompt above is preserved verbatim. It instructs the recipient not to resume existing work, modify files/code/databases/Git, or message other chats. It requests only the acknowledgement "MCP_COMPARE_20261018_01 수신" and then termination of the turn.

## Expected Behavior

Both source contexts should deliver the message to the same target thread, which should acknowledge receipt without resuming its existing work.

## Actual Results

| Source context | Tool result | Target-thread observation |
|---|---|---|
| Regular chat | isError: false | Acknowledgement received |
| Ephemeral side chat | isError: true | No new side-originated receipt was found in the two latest turns inspected |

Regular-chat response:

```json
{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"threadId\":\"01a13dfe-e475-7a52-a26d-d510bbb07869\"}"}],"isError":false}
```

The target thread then responded:

```text
MCP_COMPARE_20261018_01 수신
```

Complete side-chat response:

```json
{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"'sendRequest.bind' is not a function."}],"isError":true}
```

The outer functions.exec result was:

```text
Script completed
Wall time: 3.3 seconds
Output:
{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"'sendRequest.bind' is not a function."}],"isError":true}
```

"Script completed" indicates that the outer script finished. It does not indicate successful message delivery; the nested tool explicitly returned isError: true.

## Correlation IDs and Timestamps

- Regular source chat ID:
  01a1466a-a621-7b71-9ea6-cc17edfb26c4

- Ephemeral side chat ID:
  01a14d91-71ec-7733-9d60-252fdec4c9b1

- Target thread ID:
  01a13dfe-e475-7a52-a26d-d510bbb07869

- Successful regular-chat receipt turn ID:
  01a14e06-84ee-7660-aba0-aa6bf81c1337

- Side-chat test turn ID:
  01a14e06-e7e7-7c30-adb0-173ed7dc7f0f

- Side-chat outer call ID:
  call_e903ea62033e4683ba088feead4962fa

- Side-chat outer tool processing log timestamp:
  2026-10-18 17:00:57.067512 KST
  2026-10-18 08:00:57.067512 UTC

- Side-chat outer tool completion timestamp:
  2026-10-18 17:01:00.362818 KST
  2026-10-18 08:01:00.362818 UTC

- Target-thread inspection after the side-chat call completed:
  2026-10-18 17:01:10.661198 KST

These are timestamps for the outer functions.exec operation. The precise start time and independent request ID of the nested MCP call were not available.

## Additional Observations and Limitations

- The controlled comparison used one transmission from each source context.
- Two earlier side-chat attempts also returned the same error text.
- The controlled comparison used identical target, hostId, and prompt values.
- After the side-chat failure, the latest acknowledgement still belonged to the successful regular-chat receipt turn. It was not counted as evidence of successful side-chat delivery.
- No separate error code or stack trace was available.
- No server-side acceptance or persistence receipt was available.
- The target inspection covered the latest two turns; it does not establish permanent non-delivery or the complete internal server state.
- Separately, attempting to retrieve side-chat history returned:

```text
ephemeral threads do not support thread/turns/list
```

- The target's successful test turn only acknowledged receipt and terminated without resuming existing project work.

## Impact and Workaround

This prevents reliable message handoff from side chats to the main target thread in the observed environment.

The verified workaround is to send the message from a regular chat using the same tool.

Please investigate the client/method binding path used when send_message_to_thread is invoked from an ephemeral side chat. The exact internal failure location has not been established because no stack trace was returned. If this operation is unsupported from side chats, an explicit unsupported-operation error would be more actionable than the current binding error.

items.body:
## Summary

During an ongoing coding task, contextual approval was repeatedly rejected and the assistant resorted to asking me to copy and paste a scripted authorization sentence. That explicit sentence allowed a coordination retry, but the interruptions made a routine coding workflow unnecessarily difficult. No actionable approval button was returned with the initial denial.

## Environment

- Codex desktop app on macOS
- App version 26.1013.40934, build 20770
- Initial incident: October 18, 2026, approximately 07:10–07:22 UTC
- Coordinating conversation with a desktop coding task
- Exact macOS version, subscription tier and bundled runtime version are not included in this report.

## Observed sequence

1. During an ongoing coding task, the assistant needed to move recoverable build intermediates to an external drive, remove verified internal copies after transfer, and install and launch a source-matched test app in a simulator to capture three screenshots.
2. Three approval denials interrupted coordination. After the assistant disclosed the steps and I asked it to proceed, a coordination message was rejected before delivery.
3. The reported reason was: “The user expressed a general desire to proceed, but did not explicitly authorize this exact task message or its cache relocation/removal and simulator install side effects.”
4. No actionable approval button was returned with that denial. The assistant asked me to copy and paste a sentence explicitly enumerating the operations.
5. I supplied that explicit sentence, and the subsequent coordination retry was accepted. This does not establish that literal text matching caused the earlier denials.
6. Coordination eventually cleared. This report does not claim every approval remained blocked or that the coding work was completed.
7. When I asked to submit this problem through in-app feedback, Computer Use was rejected before the feedback interface could be inspected: “Computer Use is not allowed to use the app 'com.openai.codex' for safety reasons.” No in-app feedback receipt was obtained.
8. The sanitized report was provided to the official Help Center chatbot, but no ticket or human escalation was confirmed.

## Expected behavior

- Evaluate natural-language approval in the context of the concrete operations just disclosed.
- Preserve relevant approval context when coordinating an authorized coding task.
- If consent is insufficient, identify exactly what is missing and provide a usable action-specific approval control, ideally a one-tap option that also works comfortably from mobile.
- Avoid repeated scripted copy/paste consent when I have already approved the disclosed scope.
- Clearly distinguish missing authorization from an intentional non-overridable restriction.
- Provide a supported reporting path when the agent cannot operate the app’s feedback UI.

## Impact and investigation request

The approval loop repeatedly interrupted coding and required me to restate consent in prescribed wording. The agent could not submit in-app feedback through Computer Use.

Please investigate approval-context handling and the absence of an actionable approval control. The underlying cause is unknown. The host-app Computer Use restriction may be intentional and is reported as a feedback-path limitation, not proof of the same bug.

Related reports: #44473 and #54236. An identical root cause has not been established.

This is a sanitized account of an observed incident, not a clean-install reproduction. No private project names, repository names, local paths, account identifiers, device identifiers, credentials, raw logs or conversation transcripts are included. No weakening of security safeguards is requested.

# Intermittent MCP Apps CDP deadline before dispatch; metadata remains available

## Environment

- ChatGPT/Codex desktop 26.1013.40934, build 20770; macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Native Codex MCP Apps panel, BlueSea candidate 1.8.6, SHA256 `190fa7b64f4bc4448366278036a4714bbabbbb095e284aec23c96b1823ab1fc8`.
- Desktop local app-server uses stdio and reports 0.163.0-alpha.10.2. A separate CLI managed daemon reports 0.162.0-alpha.17.2; no evidence maps it to the failing desktop control route.
- Incident date 2026-10-18; log timestamps use UTC. Evidence assembly time is not a timestamp for each individual action.

## Expected / actual

A single documented read-only DOM request against an already-open isolated MCP Apps tab should dispatch and return or report a page-level failure. Actual: inventory/title/URL metadata can return while `playwright.evaluate` fails with `CDP operation exceeded its deadline before command dispatch`. Some longer snapshot/screenshot calls instead end in a 30-second tool timeout and runtime reset.

The same tab briefly became readable, then the dispatch failure recurred. A newly initialized empty native QA project also failed, so this is not isolated to a saved customer record. The exact internal cause, deterministic trigger and any common SDK/renderer interaction remain unproven. Please do not treat the normal revoked-session error as authorization to restore a lease.

## Reproduction and artifacts

See `MINIMAL_REPRO.md` and the three non-looping, read-only `repro/` snippets. These target the documented Codex control environment, not standalone Node. `evidence/` contains selected, sanitized existing observations and allowlisted log excerpts, not full raw logs. `MANIFEST.json` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` identify the submitted bytes. No private plugin archive, CRM data, credentials, session capabilities, usernames, conversation IDs, full transcripts or raw DOM are included.

## Recovery already attempted and stopped

Formal current-chat navigation, control-runtime reset, and formal plugin disable/enable cleanup did not restore stable DOM reads. We stopped retries. The control service was observed alive, which does not establish dispatch health. The native app automation route is explicitly prohibited; no bypass, private IPC, process kill, cache edit, auth relaxation or unrelated daemon restart was used.

## Specific request to official support

Please identify the supported recovery entry point for the desktop MCP Apps guest CDP dispatch/target-context route: either an officially exposed reset/rebind/reload action usable by the agent, or an eligible desktop/control-service fix with the exact supported application/restart procedure. No such dedicated endpoint is currently exposed to this agent. Please state whether current tab handles must be reacquired and how to preserve fail-closed session validation. A generic terminal restart instruction or restarting a separate CLI daemon does not establish a fix for this route.

If additional correlation is necessary, request a narrowly scoped field/time window through the official channel. This package intentionally pseudonymizes thread/session/init/sandbox identity and omits the full chat. Do not assume pseudonyms are real feedback session IDs. Before this issue, no ticket or feedback submission had been made.

## Acceptance after recovery

The agent, not the user, will resume same-candidate native checks after an actual official recovery event: old-page explicit reconnect with a new lease and continued old-lease rejection; isolated core business loop; inquiry/quotation audit types; native page disable/exit revocation; download/fullscreen when controllable. No production CRM writes or real email sending. Until those receipts exist, remaining native acceptance and release remain BLOCKED.

# Minimal native-host repro / 最小宿主复现

This is a report of an intermittent native-host control failure, not a guaranteed deterministic trigger or a standalone web application. The snippets require the documented Codex `cua_repl` MCP Apps environment; do not run them with Node, an external browser, raw CDP, or an app-only business tool. They have been prepared from existing observations and were not re-executed while packaging.

## Preconditions

- Desktop app 26.1013.40934 (20770), macOS arm64; environment details in `evidence/07-environment-and-health.json`.
- An already-open native BlueSea 1.8.6 MCP Apps tab, bound only to an empty disposable project. Candidate digest is recorded; the private plugin binary/source and CRM databases are not included.
- The incident had an existing revoked QA session. Do not restore it or relax validation. Business tools remain app-only.
- Prefer the existing QA tab; do not create multiple workbenches or use a real CRM project. Reusing an unrelated plugin as a platform control is only a proposed comparison, not an observed reproduction.

## Smallest read-only observation

1. Execute `repro/01-select-browser.js` as the first binding call and read the returned API documentation.
2. Execute `repro/02-select-existing-tab.js`. Bind the one observed isolated tab ID with the shown documented `tabs.get()` call. An empty inventory or ambiguous identity is a stop condition, not permission to guess or open a real project.
3. Execute `repro/03-read-dom-once.js` once. Expected: a small read-only result within the requested deadline. Recorded failure: `CDP operation exceeded its deadline before command dispatch`.
4. Preserve the single error receipt and stop. The recorded error places this request before dispatch; it is not evidence that the requested DOM callback ran and looped. Tab metadata succeeding does not prove DOM control is healthy.

The output projection omits raw body text. The prepared callback retains the recorded readyState plus bounded innerText pattern; it has not been re-executed during packaging. The snippets are intended for official support or a distinct, documented recovery event, not further retries in the current blocked state.

## Observed intermittent sequence, not an established trigger

Existing tab6 first returned `ready=complete` and an expired-session notice in about 0.15 seconds, without any restart/update/navigation. A native DOM snapshot also succeeded. One click on “确认当前项目并重新连接” yielded “正在处理…” after about 10 seconds, with no final success receipt. The next snapshot timed out at 30 seconds and reset the control runtime. Subsequent bounded DOM probes failed before dispatch. The same failure had already occurred on a newly initialized empty QA project before this click, so the click is not a proven cause.

Neither a control-runtime reset nor the earlier formal current-chat navigation restored stable control. A plugin disable/enable cleanup also did not restore DOM reads. These are recorded observations, not instructions to repeat them. Full desktop restart and unrelated CLI daemon restart were not performed.

## Evidence limits

Only native MCP Apps observations count here. Controlled React/installed-server tests are supplementary separation evidence, not native acceptance. No independent generic MCP Apps fixture has been proven to reproduce this fault. No successful screenshot was obtained in the recorded single screenshot attempt. Unique internal root cause remains undetermined. Session refusal is expected after revocation and must remain fail-closed.

# 官方提交与恢复入口

## 现有且已核对的官方入口

1. **官方反馈：当前桌面聊天输入框的 `/feedback`（或输入 `/` 选择反馈）。** 官方说明允许选择附带日志/会话，提交后才会得到反馈会话编号。本包只准备材料，尚未打开、提交或上传。不要将本包匿名 ID 当成官方反馈编号；不要自动选择完整聊天和原始日志，因为它们不在本包脱敏范围内。
2. **官方 issue 路径：桌面排障文档的 existing issues / new issue 链接。** 这是文档提供的缺陷报告路径，不是已创建工单，也不表示公开 issue 可以接收私人日志。本包已经最小化；私人补充材料仍应走官方明确指定的受控渠道。
3. **官方常规恢复说明：桌面排障文档 Terminal issues 段落。** 文档提到活动聊天结束后重启应用。这是通用终端排障建议，不能声称是本次 CDP 故障的专门修复或已执行成功。本轮也没有代替用户控制 ChatGPT 自身来执行重启。

## 真正需要官方明确或提供的恢复能力

请支持团队给出以下任一项，并明确步骤和适用版本：

- 面向当前桌面 **MCP Apps guest CDP 派发 / target-context** 的正式 reset / rebind / reload 入口，且可由代理使用；或
- 修复该通路的官方桌面/控制服务版本，以及通过官方更新器应用修复的操作与重启条件。

这是向官方提出的恢复请求，**不是宣称上述专门入口已经存在**。当前代理接口没有暴露它。`cua_repl.js_reset` 只清除控制运行时绑定；`codex doctor` 只出诊断报告；`codex app` 只启动应用。单独 CLI managed daemon 与当前桌面 stdio 链路没有已证实的对应关系，不能把重启它作为本故障修复。

Computer Use 官方规则禁止自动化 ChatGPT 自身；不更换 App 标识、使用系统事件、私有 IPC、杀进程、降低安全设置或修改插件绕过限制。应用工具本身仍须严格校验项目、版本、会话和绑定，旧授权保持撤销。

## 停止重试与恢复后的接续

本次打包未调用任何原生控制、opener、会话签发或业务写工具。没有轮询、定时重试或后台监控。只在官方提供实际恢复动作、官方修复版本应用完成，或宿主明确报告新的可用控制入口之后，由代理执行一次有界健康检查；失败即新增一份回执并停止，不让用户代测。

一次 DOM 读取成功只表示可以开始验收，不等于稳定恢复或业务通过。后续必须完成 `RESUME_ACCEPTANCE.md` 的原生动作与回读。新授权只来自明确重新连接；不恢复任何旧租约。没有设置后台自动接续任务，本包保留下一次恢复事件后的执行交接。

## 核对来源（2026-10-18）

- [官方桌面排障：反馈、日志、通用恢复](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/troubleshooting)
- [官方命令：/feedback 收集并提交所选诊断](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands)

# Intermittent MCP Apps CDP deadline before dispatch; metadata remains available

## Environment

- ChatGPT/Codex desktop 26.1013.40934, build 20770; macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Native Codex MCP Apps panel, BlueSea candidate 1.8.6, SHA256 `190fa7b64f4bc4448366278036a4714bbabbbb095e284aec23c96b1823ab1fc8`.
- Desktop local app-server uses stdio and reports 0.163.0-alpha.10.2. A separate CLI managed daemon reports 0.162.0-alpha.17.2; no evidence maps it to the failing desktop control route.
- Incident date 2026-10-18; log timestamps use UTC. Evidence assembly time is not a timestamp for each individual action.

## Expected / actual

A single documented read-only DOM request against an already-open isolated MCP Apps tab should dispatch and return or report a page-level failure. Actual: inventory/title/URL metadata can return while `playwright.evaluate` fails with `CDP operation exceeded its deadline before command dispatch`. Some longer snapshot/screenshot calls instead end in a 30-second tool timeout and runtime reset.

The same tab briefly became readable, then the dispatch failure recurred. A newly initialized empty native QA project also failed, so this is not isolated to a saved customer record. The exact internal cause, deterministic trigger and any common SDK/renderer interaction remain unproven. Please do not treat the normal revoked-session error as authorization to restore a lease.

## Reproduction and artifacts

See `MINIMAL_REPRO.md` and the three non-looping, read-only `repro/` snippets. These target the documented Codex control environment, not standalone Node. `evidence/` contains selected, sanitized existing observations and allowlisted log excerpts, not full raw logs. `MANIFEST.json` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` identify the submitted bytes. No private plugin archive, CRM data, credentials, session capabilities, usernames, conversation IDs, full transcripts or raw DOM are included.

## Recovery already attempted and stopped

Formal current-chat navigation, control-runtime reset, and formal plugin disable/enable cleanup did not restore stable DOM reads. We stopped retries. The control service was observed alive, which does not establish dispatch health. The native app automation route is explicitly prohibited; no bypass, private IPC, process kill, cache edit, auth relaxation or unrelated daemon restart was used.

## Specific request to official support

Please identify the supported recovery entry point for the desktop MCP Apps guest CDP dispatch/target-context route: either an officially exposed reset/rebind/reload action usable by the agent, or an eligible desktop/control-service fix with the exact supported application/restart procedure. No such dedicated endpoint is currently exposed to this agent. Please state whether current tab handles must be reacquired and how to preserve fail-closed session validation. A generic terminal restart instruction or restarting a separate CLI daemon does not establish a fix for this route.

If additional correlation is necessary, request a narrowly scoped field/time window through the official channel. This package intentionally pseudonymizes thread/session/init/sandbox identity and omits the full chat. Do not assume pseudonyms are real feedback session IDs; no ticket or feedback submission has been made.

## Acceptance after recovery

The agent, not the user, will resume same-candidate native checks after an actual official recovery event: old-page explicit reconnect with a new lease and continued old-lease rejection; isolated core business loop; inquiry/quotation audit types; native page disable/exit revocation; download/fullscreen when controllable. No production CRM writes or real email sending. Until those receipts exist, remaining native acceptance and release remain BLOCKED.
