items.title: [macOS] Concurrent chats show synchronized HTTPS/SSE and WebSocket failures with local router stopped

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Desktop host `26.1013.40934`, build `20770`, verified from the installed bundle's Info.plist. Its actual running bundled app-server executable reports `codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2`. The About dialog was not used.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT subscription authentication, not an API key. The billing UI tier was not independently verified for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS `27.2`, Apple Silicon. `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 27.2.0 arm64 arm`.

### What issue are you seeing?

Three concurrent existing local coding chats encounter nearly simultaneous request/response transport failures. The user sees repeated `Reconnecting 1/5` or `2/5` between otherwise successful tool actions in two chats. A third chat did not show a visible failure, although its request-level errors are present in the native logs and recovered within the same turn.

This is an observational report of **correlated transport errors**, not a claim that all three turns failed permanently or that a particular component caused the disconnections.

The following direct-connection control was verified before correlating the events:

- A previously used local model-routing gateway was fully closed; its process was absent and its loopback health endpoint was unavailable.
- The desktop app was then restarted. New native logs show direct OpenAI endpoints, rather than the old localhost gateway.
- Two chats use HTTPS Responses (`https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`); another attempts secure WebSocket Responses (`wss://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`). A history-compatible HTTP provider entry remains for existing chats, pointing directly to the same OpenAI backend with WebSockets disabled. Thus the HTTPS arm is not claimed to be an untouched default-provider configuration.
- The model recorded in the affected spans is `gpt-6.1-sol`; `max` and `ultra` effort values occur in the sampled window.

Two clusters on **2026-10-18, UTC**:

| Native log time | Chat A: direct HTTPS | Chat B: direct HTTPS | Chat C: direct WebSocket |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 07:33:34 | `error sending request` | `Transport error: network error: error decoding response body` | `IO error: peer closed connection without sending TLS close_notify` |
| 07:33:53 | `error sending request` | `Transport error: network error: error decoding response body` | `IO error: peer closed connection without sending TLS close_notify` |

Chat B received HTTP 200 headers before its body-consumption errors. Chats B and C logged sampling retries `1/5` and `2/5`; those counters are not counts of terminal failed turns. Chat A received HTTP 200 on subsequent requests in the same turn and continued working without a visible error. HTTP 200 alone is not treated as proof that a response stream completed.

These failures are recorded under ordinary `turn_input` / `session_task.run` / `run_turn` operations. No direct start, completion or failure event for client compaction was found for these turns in the sampled interval, 07:33:10–07:40:00 UTC. The inspected limit checks were below their effective compaction threshold. This does not exclude opaque server-side/in-stream behavior or other context-dependent failures.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed workflow; **not a deterministic minimal reproduction**:

1. Sign in with ChatGPT in the macOS desktop app and continue several established local coding chats using tools.
2. Run three chats concurrently over the same network/proxy setup.
3. Observe successful tool actions followed by repeated sampling reconnects in some chats.
4. Correlate native logs across the chats: the response-body, TLS-close and request-send errors above occur at the same logged second, including after a full desktop restart with the local model-routing gateway stopped.

There were also successful requests between failures. A controlled single-chat versus three-chat comparison and a proxy-free comparison have **not** been completed. No causal claim is made about concurrency or context size. Private prompts, repository contents, thread/turn IDs and raw logs are omitted.

### What is the expected behavior?

Parallel chats should continue reliably or recover with clear per-request diagnostics. When several chats disconnect at once, diagnostics should make it possible to distinguish response truncation/content decoding, TLS/connection termination, client cancellation and upstream processing failures, and correlate retries with the originating requests.

### Additional information

- A system HTTP/HTTPS proxy and Shadowrocket VPN remained active during the direct-OpenAI control. “Direct” here means **bypassing the local model router**, not bypassing the VPN or using an unproxied Internet connection. Network/proxy and upstream causes remain possible.
- macOS `configd` recorded network-configuration notifications at 07:33:16 and 07:33:17 UTC, including IPv4/IPv6, DNS and proxy categories, before the first error cluster. The inspected window did not show an explicit physical Wi-Fi link-down or VPN connection-state transition. Before/after setting values and flow-level attribution were not captured, so these notifications are a possible confound, not an established cause. A later manual VPN reconnection occurred after the two clusters and is excluded from this comparison.
- User-level context overrides are `model_context_window = 1000000` and `model_auto_compact_token_limit = 900000`. They are disclosed as non-default configuration, not proposed as a cause. No proxy/CA environment variables, explicit transport-timeout overrides or `respect_system_proxy` override were found in the inspected running desktop/native processes and current Codex configuration.
- Earlier failures also occurred through the local model router, but its locally generated 502/503 errors and translated stream errors are deliberately not presented as native OpenAI service errors in this report.
- This report includes no newly submitted in-app feedback upload. Sanitized local timing/endpoint evidence is retained; please advise which supported private diagnostics or request identifiers would help correlate the failing requests.
- Related: #43767 (synchronized retry waves), #49540 (HTTP/SSE decode failures despite WebSockets being disabled), and #38969 (compaction failures and reports of ordinary-generation failures). These are symptom overlaps; an identical root cause is not established.

Agent-assisted report posted at the affected user's explicit request.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1013.4894.0 (installed Windows package; exact About-dialog version unavailable)

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT subscription (plan not verified)

### What platform is your computer?

Windows, 64-bit

### What issue are you seeing?

After a Codex Desktop update, the entire local Projects list became empty. Existing conversations still appear in Recents and retain their working directories, but the project list is empty and the app API returns an empty collection from `list_projects`.

Previous investigation found that historical project/task associations existed before the update. Attempts to reconstruct project metadata were overwritten by the app after restart. Restarting Codex and re-opening the application did not restore the project list.

This resembles open reports #35088 and #39121: a Windows Desktop project-registry/sidebar synchronization or migration failure rather than loss of workspace files.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use Codex Desktop on Windows with existing local projects and conversations.
2. Update or restart the desktop application.
3. Open the Projects section.
4. Observe that it is empty.
5. Check Recents: previous conversations remain available.
6. Call `list_projects`: it returns an empty `projects` collection.

### What is the expected behavior?

Historical local projects and their conversation groupings remain visible after an update or restart.

### Additional information

No workspace folders were intentionally removed. Existing conversations remain available, so the project organization appears to be missing rather than the underlying task data.
